- [fix] **`dan-up` no longer kills a healthy server just because local startup takes slightly longer than 15 seconds.** Root-cause reproduction showed the launcher’s `wait_for_health()` logic in `src/dan/cli/up.py` was using a brittle fixed delay table that gave up at 15s, while the local server was becoming healthy at about 15.1s. That meant `dan-up` printed “Server failed to start within timeout” and then immediately SIGTERM’d a server that had already completed startup or was about to pass `/health`. The launcher now polls `/health` against a real deadline (`25s`, `0.5s` interval) instead of a hard-coded delay list, and added focused unit coverage in `tests/test_cli/test_up.py`.
- [refactor] **Removed hard-coded write-file stagnation counters; replaced with prompt-driven incremental writing and same-family parallel tool restriction.** The old `_WRITE_FILE_STAGNATION_TURNS` / `_WRITE_FILE_STAGNATION_TURNS_RESEARCH` counters and associated `non_write_stagnation_turns` / `force_file_write` escalation logic were removed. The model now gets guidance upfront via the system prompt instead:
  1. **System prompt teaches incremental writing**: `_RESEARCH_REPORT_PROMPT_HINT` now has three explicit phases — Research (batch same-family search/read calls where appropriate), Structure (outline before writing), Incremental Writing (mandatory chunk-by-chunk file_write with mode='overwrite' then mode='append', ~1500-2500 chars per chunk). The general tool guidance now also says to outline long files first and write one bounded chunk at a time. The existing `missing_target → force_file_write` path (for "file not found" errors) is retained.
  2. **Non-contradictory action prompts**: `_tool_retry_prompt_for_missing_actions` now detects both `search_web + write_file` and `read_file + write_file` combinations and gives a consistent ordering ("research/read FIRST, then write incrementally") instead of contradictory instructions.
  3. **Parallel tool calls restricted to same-family batches**: `asyncio.gather` in the tool execution loop now groups consecutive calls by a small family map (`read`, `grep`, `search`) and runs only those same-family groups in parallel; mixed families still execute sequentially. This prevents incoherent mixed parallel execution (for example `web_search + file_write`) while still allowing productive batches (for example `file_read + pdf_read`, or multiple `web_search` calls).
  Replaced stagnation regression tests with `test_same_family_read_calls_run_in_parallel` and `test_mixed_type_tool_calls_run_sequentially_by_group`, and added prompt regressions including `test_prompt_guidance_uses_overwrite_for_first_chunk`.
- [fix] **Heartbeat progress updates no longer cancel the in-flight model call they are meant to protect.** Root-cause debugging of the repeated “response stream ended” failures showed `_iter_guarded_complete()` in `src/dan/server/chat_manager.py` was cancelling *all* pending tasks after every 8-second wait timeout, which accidentally included the live `provider.complete()` task whenever `emit_progress_ack=True`. That self-inflicted cancellation then surfaced as `Guarded completion cancelled unexpectedly`, degraded the turn into raw tool output, or fell through to the outer synthesized fallback. The wait loop now leaves the in-flight completion task running across heartbeat timeouts and only cancels the transient helper tasks. Added a focused regression in `tests/test_server/test_multi_turn_tools.py`.
- [fix] **Unexpected provider-side cancellations no longer escape the guarded completion path and degrade into the outer “response stream ended” fallback.** `src/dan/server/chat_manager.py` now treats `asyncio.CancelledError` from `provider.complete()` as an internal failure when the current task itself was not externally cancelled and the stream stop-event was not set. In that case it logs the request shape (`model`, message count, tools, `emit_progress_ack`) and converts the cancellation into a normal runtime failure that the existing tool-loop fallback path can surface as a terminal response. Added a focused regression in `tests/test_server/test_multi_turn_tools.py`.
- [fix] **Post-tool follow-up failures now leave a diagnostic trail instead of only a generic outer fallback.** `src/dan/server/chat_manager.py` now logs when the multi-turn tool loop starts its follow-up completion (`tools`, missing required actions, `force_file_write`, last downstream stream channel, context size) and, crucially, logs the emitted inner step trace when that guarded completion exits without a `CompletionResult`. This makes silent early exits after successful tool calls debuggable from the server log rather than only appearing later as the synthesized “response stream ended” fallback. Added a focused regression in `tests/test_server/test_multi_turn_tools.py`.
- [fix] **Chat stream producers now synthesize a terminal fallback if an event stream ends silently before any real terminal event is sent.** `src/dan/server/app.py` now tracks whether `/api/chat/message` emitted a terminal `chat_complete` / `chat_error` / `chat_interrupted` / `chat_mutation` (excluding `progress_ack`) and injects a fallback `chat_complete` when an inner event stream stops after tool progress but before final output. This hardens both tiered and non-tiered paths at the outer stream boundary so reconnects can recover a terminal snapshot instead of degrading into the “backend restarted or forgot this live response stream” banner. Added a focused regression in `tests/test_server/test_chat_integration.py`.
- [fix] **Tiered executor streams now synthesize a terminal response when a wrapped handler exits after tool events without a final `chat_complete` / `chat_interrupted`.** `src/dan/server/concierge/tier_executors.py` now detects this anomaly in both Tier 1 and Tier 2 leaf execution paths, logs it, and emits a fallback terminal completion instead of silently ending the session. This prevents the UI from being left with a dead reconnect-only stream after partial tool progress. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_concierge/test_tiered_dispatch.py`.
- [fix] **Tool-heavy chat turns now keep a textual progress line visible alongside tool cards instead of dropping to tool pills only.** `editor/src/lib/toolCallPresentation.ts` now derives readable status text from the latest tool event (`Listing directory contents of src`, `Finished web search … Continuing...`, etc.), and `ChatPanel.tsx` applies that text on both `chat_tool_call_start` and `chat_tool_call_result` so the assistant bubble still explains the current step while tools are executing.
- [fix] **Tiered-dispatch follow-up correctness: pending confirm replies now replay through the tiered path itself, and root assistant turns now actually persist `session_tree` metadata.** `src/dan/server/concierge/tiered_dispatch.py` now consults the legacy `_resolve_pending_follow_up()` helper before triage so `"yes"` / clarification replies resume the original action without silently depending on a legacy fallback. `src/dan/server/concierge/models.py` adds optional `TaskTurn.metadata`, `runtime.py` lets `_record_assistant_turn()` accept metadata, and `tiered_dispatch.py` now routes root assistant persistence through that helper while attaching the full `session_tree` trace and still storing memory candidates. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_concierge/test_tiered_dispatch.py`; the full tracked Plan 34 suite now passes (`19 passed`).
- [feat] **Tiered dispatch now shares the runtime progress session and propagates root cancellation through child execution.** `src/dan/server/concierge/runtime.py` now initializes tiered runs through the same `ProgressSession` helper used by the legacy path, and `_make_phase_event()` emits immediate updates for real phase transitions while still throttling same-phase churn. `src/dan/server/concierge/tiered_dispatch.py` now emits intake/context/execution phase events on the tiered path, and `src/dan/server/concierge/tier_executors.py` now runs child sessions with subtask-scoped messages, lazily spawns serial children, bubbles child tool/final events, and stops the session tree promptly when `cancel_event` is set. Added deterministic coverage in `tests/test_concierge/test_tiered_dispatch.py` for Tier 0, Tier 1 phase emission, Tier 2 child bubbling, and cancellation.
- [feat] **Triage post-processing now resolves entities, normalizes context needs, and fills resume targets before tiered dispatch.** `src/dan/server/concierge/triage.py` now dedupes packed `context_needs` tokens (for example `memory/file:/path/domain:x/reuse`), maps project/task/workflow/file entity labels onto known IDs using the resolved context plus optional `ProjectStore`, and uses resume cues plus `ResumeProtocol` candidate scans to set `resume_task_id` when possible. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_concierge/test_triage.py`, and `src/dan/server/concierge/tiered_dispatch.py` now passes `project_store` into `triage()` so the live tiered path gets the store-backed resolution behavior.
- [test] **Completed the remaining SessionManager coverage for plan 34-1 with focused lifecycle/tree tests.** Added `tests/test_concierge/test_session_manager.py` covering root creation + env-loaded limits, SINGLE-tier child rejection, depth/child/total budget enforcement, state transitions with timestamps, cancellation/pruning behavior, trace generation, and nested tree export. Verified with `pytest tests/test_concierge/test_session_manager.py -q` (`8` passing); no `src/dan/server/concierge/session.py` patch was needed.
- [fix] **Multi-turn tool execution now retries only explicitly retryable capability failures and forces stalled write tasks toward `file_write`.** `src/dan/server/chat_manager.py` now performs one bounded internal retry only when a capability handler returns `retryable=True`, detects repeated read-only turns (`file_read` / `file_grep` / `list_directory`) while `write_file` remains unsatisfied, and immediately pivots toward `file_write` when a write-oriented task hits a missing-target read failure (`File not found`, `Directory not found`, similar `error_type`s). Added focused regressions in `tests/test_server/test_multi_turn_tools.py`, and the existing required-action handoff suite still passes.
- [fix] **Editor chat-stream reconnect logic no longer retries terminally closed channels after a clean close.** `editor/src/lib/chatStreamLifecycle.ts` now short-circuits reconnects for WebSocket close codes `1000`, `1005`, and terminally missing `4004` before any transport-error hint can mark the stream as transient. This prevents terminal snapshot replay loops that kept reopening finished chat channels and eventually devolved into repeated `4004` reconnect churn. Added a focused regression in `editor/src/lib/__tests__/chatStreamLifecycle.test.ts`.
- [fix] **`shell_command` capability no longer mislabels successful commands as failures.** `handle_shell_command()` in `src/dan/server/capability_handlers.py` was reading `return_code`, but `dan.tools.shell_command` returns `exit_code`. That made successful commands show `exit code: -1` and propagate as failed capability calls even when stdout was correct. The handler now reads `exit_code` with `return_code` as a backward-compatible fallback and fills `output_preview` consistently. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_server/test_shell_command_capability.py`.
- [refactor] **Extracted 1210-line legacy sequential processing path from `_process_inner` into `_legacy_process_inner`.** `_process_inner` is now a 25-line clean router: fast command → tiered dispatch → legacy fallback. The legacy path (heuristic cascade, classification, guards, solver, goal orchestrator) is fully preserved but isolated, making the architecture boundary explicit. Also fixed 8 bugs across the new tiered modules: `SessionResult.duration` → `duration_ms` (5 sites), `InstantExecutor` invalid PENDING→COMPLETED transition, `triage()` crash on `llm_complete=None`, `ResolvedContext()` no-args crash, `_root_sessions` keyed by empty `surface_id` → `external_id`, child sessions not inheriting `msg`/`context` from parent, double context resolution in `_do_triage` + `gather`, missing `_finalize_task`/`_save_concierge_state` in root completion.
- [feat] **TieredDispatcher integration layer wired into ConciergeRuntime behind `DAN_TIERED_DISPATCH` feature flag (plan 34-4, tasks 1-5b).** New `src/dan/server/concierge/tiered_dispatch.py` with `ContextGatherer` (triage-guided context fetching replacing speculative parallel prep — only fetches memory, files, domain, reuse when triage `context_needs` requests them) and `TieredDispatcher` (central coordinator: triage -> gather context -> dispatch to tier executor -> per-session telemetry -> root-session conversation turn recording + aggregated telemetry + session pruning). `runtime.py` patched with `_TIERED_DISPATCH` env flag, `__init__` initialization block (creates `SessionManager`, wires `InstantExecutor`/`SingleShotExecutor`/`MultiStepExecutor`, with try/except fallback), and `_process_inner` branch after fast-command check that delegates to the dispatcher with graceful fallback to the standard path on failure. Event streaming, progress emission, cancellation wiring, and tests remain pending (tasks 6-11).
- [feat] **Tier executors for tiered async dispatcher (plan 34-3).** New `src/dan/server/concierge/tier_executors.py` with `TierExecutor` protocol, `InstantExecutor` (Tier 0 — social turns, pending follow-ups), `SingleShotExecutor` (Tier 1 — single handler call Q&A/lookups), and `MultiStepExecutor` (Tier 2 — recursive decompose-or-execute with parallel/serial child execution, tier estimation heuristic, queue-based event interleaving, all-children-failed fallback, and simple synthesis). Uses TYPE_CHECKING imports for session module to avoid circular deps. Tasks 1-12 of plan 34-3.
- [feat] **Session model and SessionManager for tiered async dispatcher (plan 34-1).** New `src/dan/server/concierge/session.py` with `SessionTier` (INSTANT/SINGLE/MULTI), `SessionState` (7-state machine with enforced transitions), `SessionResult`, `SessionTrace`, `Session` (Pydantic v2 with tree structure, depth/budget limits from env vars), and `SessionManager` (in-memory tree tracker with `create_root`, `create_child`, state transitions, `can_spawn_child` budget enforcement, `cancel_tree`, `prune_completed`, `build_trace`, `export_tree`). Tasks 1-8 of plan 34-1 complete; unit tests (task 9) still pending.
- [refactor] **Unified chat prompt guidance is now compact, registry-backed, and conditional instead of globally over-specific.** `chat_manager.py` now replaces the stale hardcoded tool list (and leftover `{mcp_block}` placeholder) with a compact live tool-family summary from the registered tools, injects research/report guidance only for research-like asks instead of every turn, assembles the final system prompt from explicit sections rather than repeated string concatenation, makes build clarification prompts domain-agnostic, and deduplicates WhatsApp surface-hint text. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_chat_manager_prompt_design.py`.
- [fix] **Required-action tool enforcement now escalates to the exact missing tool when only one concrete tool remains, and reconnect snapshots no longer treat progress heartbeats as terminal completions.** `chat_manager.py` now keeps generic `tool_choice="required"` while multiple action paths remain possible, but when the only unmet action maps to a single concrete tool (for example `write_file` → `file_write`) and the provider supports exact tool targeting, it sends a provider-level function-specific `tool_choice` instead of relying on the model to infer the last step. This replaces the earlier temporary read-budget heuristic and keeps repeated chunked file reads allowed. `chat_stream_buffer.py` now skips `progress_ack` events when capturing terminal reconnect snapshots, so long-running tool turns do not reconnect-loop on stale heartbeat completions. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_chat_manager_tool_handoff.py`.
- [fix] **Chat now loads the most recently used thread by default, auto-focuses the input on navigation, and shows live progress status during tool execution.** `chat_store.py` `list_threads` now returns threads sorted by `updated_at` descending so the frontend picks up the latest thread instead of the first-created one. `ChatPanel.tsx` auto-focuses the textarea after new-chat, load-thread, and empty-state transitions. `progress_ack` events are now stored in a separate `progressStatus` field on the assistant message and rendered as an animated status pill below tool calls, instead of silently replacing the accumulated response content.
- [fix] **Entity grounding now uses word-boundary matching for single-word project labels ≥3 chars** (`entity_grounding.py`). Previously, `norm_label in norm_text` matched substrings ("data" in "database", "test" in "testing"), causing false project matches that cascaded into incorrect short-circuit responses and guard triggers. Single-word labels now use word-set membership; multi-word labels still use phrase substring match.
- [fix] **Narrowed `_ABOUT_PROJECT_PHRASES` and added action-verb exclusion** (`entity_grounding.py`). Removed ambiguous verbs ("update", "review", "check on", "where is") that triggered false `is_about_project` short-circuits when users wanted action ("update the report", "review this code"). Added `_ACTION_VERB_PHRASES` set so "update the X" / "review the X" / "check the X" are excluded from status-query detection.
- [fix] **Non-build fast path now checks policy for destructive actions and runs response relevance guard** (`runtime.py`). Previously, ask/agent intents with confidence ≥0.7 skipped all guardrails including CONFIRM policy (allowing "delete the workflow" to bypass confirmation) and response relevance (letting misrouted answers go unchecked). Now runs `resolve_policy()` and falls through to the full pipeline if CONFIRM is needed, and appends Guard 3 relevance hints to responses.
- [fix] **Solver confidence is now parsed from LLM response instead of hardcoded to 0.85** (`solver.py`). Added `confidence` field to the solver system prompt and JSON template. `_parse_llm_response` now reads the LLM's confidence when available (falling back to 0.7), giving Guard 2 (understanding coherence) a real signal instead of a meaningless constant.
- [fix] **Handler errors now surface to the user instead of being silently swallowed** (`executor.py`). When all handlers fail (primary + fallback chain), the last error type and message are included in the partial-result response so users know what went wrong instead of getting a vague "I wasn't able to complete the task" message.
- [fix] **Deduplicated memory retrieval on the solver path** (`runtime.py`). Previously, `_retrieve_memory_context` could run 3 times per turn (parallel prep, project refresh, solver path). Now the third call is skipped when the project ID was already covered by earlier retrieval.
- [fix] **Correction detection skipped for new conversations** (`runtime.py`). Previously, `detect_correction()` ran on every non-fast-path message even with no conversation history. Now requires ≥2 turns before correction detection runs. Also reduced correction-to-domain-knowledge importance from 0.8 to 0.5 to prevent single corrections from dominating domain context.
- [refactor] **Long-horizon orchestration now carries the same bounded goal contract used by concierge direct-task execution.** Added `src/dan/meta/goal_contract.py` as a shared normalization/rendering helper, persisted a normalized `goal_contract` on long-horizon `ConciergeGoal.context`, and threaded it into `MetaSession.goal_context` so `WorkflowPlanner.plan()` sees explicit goal, deliverable, constraints, required actions, completion checks, and next step during planning/replanning. The inline intent-extraction path now injects the same contract into `extract_workflow_intent()` prompts, and `goal_loop.py` can render the contract inside strategy-tier prompts when present. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_meta/test_goal_contract.py`.
- [refactor] **Concierge routing now carries an explicit deliberation contract, and direct-task completion gates are based on successful required actions instead of mere tool attempts.** `src/dan/server/concierge/classifier.py` now accepts richer LLM route payloads (`target`, `action_hints`, `goal`, `deliverable`, `constraints`, `next_step`), stores a bounded `deliberation` object on `ClassificationResult`, and removes the older broad status/external-fact phrase bags from the primary routing path. `src/dan/server/concierge/handlers.py` now injects an execution-contract block into concierge tool prompts so the model re-checks goal, deliverable, required actions, and completion criteria before acting. `src/dan/server/chat_manager.py` now treats `read_file` / `search_web` / `write_file` as satisfied only after successful tool completion, retries failed required actions instead of accepting them as done, and refuses to finalize when the last required action is still missing. Added regressions in `tests/test_classifier.py` and `tests/test_chat_manager_tool_handoff.py`.
- [refactor] **Concierge classifier now uses a minimal `ask` / `agent` / `plan` route taxonomy instead of the older intent enum sprawl.** `src/dan/server/concierge/classifier.py` and `intent_catalog.py` now classify only into the three top-level routes, with `route.target` / `action_hints` carrying the remaining detail. `runtime.py`, `handlers.py`, `policy.py`, `solver.py`, and `executor.py` were rewired around the smaller surface via new `AskHandler` / `AgentHandler` / `PlanHandler` dispatch, while keeping file lookup, status lookup, run control, publish, workflow edit, and long-horizon meta-goal behavior available behind route hints instead of legacy intent names. Updated regressions in `tests/test_classifier.py` and `tests/test_domain_learning.py`.
- [fix] **Classifier routing is now LLM-first with a structured intent catalog, and reconnectable chat streams keep their terminal state long enough to survive reconnects.** Extracted the routing ontology into `src/dan/server/concierge/intent_catalog.py`, changed `classify_intent_llm()` to always ask the classifier LLM first and only fall back to the scored heuristic when the model fails/returns garbage, and now parse LLM confidence/reason into `ClassificationResult`. On the stream side, `/api/chat/{channel}/events` now accepts missing channels before closing with WebSocket code `4004` (instead of an HTTP 403 handshake rejection) and preserves chat stream mappings whenever a producer is still alive or a recoverable terminal snapshot exists. Added regressions in `tests/test_classifier.py` and `tests/test_chat_stream_buffer.py`.
- [fix] **Classifier routing is now score-based instead of a brittle first-match regex waterfall.** `src/dan/server/concierge/classifier.py` now extracts semantic features (path presence, retrieval vs artifact intent, workflow-edit cues, status/run-control, experience/publish signals, direct web lookup) and scores all `IntentCategory` candidates before choosing the winner. Confidence is derived from the top-vs-second score gap instead of fixed per-branch constants. The LLM classifier prompt was also updated so path-scoped read/transform/write tasks classify as `direct_task` rather than `file_request`. Added regression coverage in `tests/test_classifier.py` for path-scoped read+analyze, write-to-path, read-change-write, complex report-in-folder, explicit file retrieval, recent file follow-up, and handler-side explicit-path context handling. Also patched `DirectTaskHandler._references_file_without_context()` so an explicit path in the current message counts as sufficient context instead of forcing a bogus clarification.
- [fix] **`_continue_or_new` now uses micro-tier LLM for ambiguous follow-up detection instead of hardcoded keywords.** Deterministic keyword matching is preserved for unambiguous UI commands (yes/no, pause, start over, run it, etc.) and build-session contexts. For free-text messages where it's unclear whether they continue the active goal or start a new task, an LLM call with the active goal description decides CONTINUE vs NEW. Falls back to "new" on LLM failure. This replaces the previous keyword set which missed natural follow-ups like "make it faster" or novel phrasings.
- [fix] **Concierge goal state persistence: 7 chain-breaking bugs in the concierge loop.** End-to-end review of the concierge goal execution path revealed several scenarios where complex tasks could silently fail or lose state. (1) `_execute_goal_inline` silent failures on intent extraction and graph build now annotate goal context with failure reason so MetaController fallback has visibility. (2) INTERACTIVE autonomy pause now persists goal state immediately via `_upsert_goal` + `_save_concierge_state` before returning, so paused inline graphs survive crashes. (3) Non-exception run failures (`run_result.success == False`) and exception failures in `Engine.run()` now persist failed goal state immediately instead of relying on the caller. (4) Event queue drain loop now has a configurable timeout (`DAN_INLINE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT`, default 600s) with task cancellation, preventing indefinite hangs on engine deadlocks. (5) Goal orchestrator inline+MetaController cascade wrapped in try/finally so `_upsert_goal` + `_save_concierge_state` always execute even on unexpected exceptions. (6) Reuse prompt now saves goal to `active_goals` before returning, so goals survive session closure while awaiting user reply. (7) `_continue_or_new` follow-up detection replaced with LLM-based approach (see above). (8) MetaController exception handler no longer calls `_sync_goal_from_session` with the stale pre-execution session object. (9) Reuse failure context (`plan_action = "generate"`) now updates `goal.updated_at` before falling through. (10) Repair cap check now catches "paused" goals at max iterations and records the cap reason in `error_history`.
- [test] **Cycle 3 eval battery (post-33-10, build lane).** 56 records, 25.0% honest pass rate (down from 46.7% Cycle 2 structural-only). Fixture enforcement (33-10 B) revealed 23 expectation_mismatch failures — graphs that previously "passed" but don't match prompt intent. Intent compiler activation up to 30.4% (T1=63.6%, T2=75.0%). T1 improved to 54.5%, T4 to 40.0%. Main issues: intent compiler under-noding (9 single-node graphs for multi-step prompts), multi-turn mutation stagnation (0/10 follow-ups grow graphs), T5 edge case misrouting (5/6 build when shouldn't). Results: `tests/eval/results/2026-03-13_002753_run.jsonl`.

## 2026-03-12
- [fix] **Final chat-thread saves now supersede older debounced snapshots instead of being overwritten by them a few seconds later.** `ChatPanel.tsx` used one immediate persistence path for terminal `chat_complete`/`chat_interrupted`/`chat_mutation` events and a separate debounced autosave path for partial milestones like attachments, tool updates, and run events. The debounced snapshot was not cancelled when a newer immediate save for the same thread landed, so an older delayed payload could still flush afterward and clobber the latest saved assistant state. Extracted `editor/src/lib/threadPersistenceCoordinator.ts` to coordinate scheduled vs immediate saves and added Vitest coverage in `editor/src/lib/__tests__/threadPersistenceCoordinator.test.ts`.
- [fix] **Context compaction now strips orphan tool messages, and tool-loop cancellation is locked in with late-branch regressions.** `_compact_context()` now sanitizes malformed transcripts before budgeting so stray `tool` messages cannot survive into later follow-up completions without a preceding assistant `tool_calls` message. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_chat_context_compaction.py`, plus new cancellation tests in `tests/test_server/test_multi_turn_tools.py` that prove `cancel_event` interrupts in-flight continuation, post-tool follow-up, and forced cap-synthesis completions instead of drifting into a normal terminal response.
- [fix] **Chat recovery banners now auto-scroll into view instead of hiding behind the composer.** The live restart smoke test showed the new disconnect/retry banner could render below the current scroll position because `ChatPanel.tsx` only auto-scrolled on message changes. Added a follow-up scroll effect for `error` and stale-revision banners so recovery actions stay visible the moment they appear.
- [fix] **Desktop chat disconnects now explain local backend restarts and recover the latest saved thread snapshot when possible.** `ChatPanel.tsx` now treats short socket failures as retryable with exponential backoff, probes a lightweight `/api/health` endpoint to distinguish generic stream loss from a temporarily unavailable local DAN backend, and reloads the persisted thread after restart-driven stream loss so the user sees the freshest saved partial response instead of a stale "disconnected" bubble.
- [fix] **Post-tool terminal answers now retain any spawned `run-*` handoff, including forced cap-synthesis exits.** The first pass of the turn-cap patch already forced one no-tools partial synthesis when `max_tool_turns` was reached, but the terminal `ChatCompleteEvent` still dropped `last_stream_channel_id` in the normal completion, continuation-failure, and cap-synthesis branches. Fixed by threading `stream_channel_id=last_stream_channel_id` through all post-tool terminal completion paths so tool-triggered runs can continue streaming into the client even after the chat loop finalizes. Added regressions in `tests/test_chat_manager_tool_handoff.py`.
- [fix] **Tool-turn cap now degrades into a bounded partial synthesis instead of a raw stop message.** When `send_message_with_tools()` hits `max_tool_turns` and the model still wants more tools, it now makes one final no-tools synthesis call based only on already gathered context, then appends an explicit note that the answer may be partial because the tool-call limit was reached. If that bounded synthesis fails, the runtime still falls back to the prior cap note. Added regression coverage in `tests/test_chat_manager_tool_handoff.py`.
- [fix] **Chat stream reconnects now keep a bounded recoverable tail, and SQLite telemetry no longer drops parameter-decision fields.** `app.py` no longer uses plain unbounded `asyncio.Queue()` instances for chat/run handoff streams; it now routes events through `ReconnectableChatStream` in `src/dan/server/chat_stream_buffer.py`, which coalesces detached token spam, bounds buffered events while no consumer is attached, and keeps a replayable terminal snapshot so reconnects can still recover the tail even after the producer task has already exited. Also updated `SQLiteTelemetryStore` to add/migrate `parameter_key` and `parameter_value` columns and include them in inserts, so `ParameterDecisionLogger` round-trips correctly in the default DB-backed telemetry path. Added regressions in `tests/test_chat_stream_buffer.py` and `tests/test_sqlite_telemetry_store.py`.
- [fix] **Run-stream handoffs now reconnect like chat streams, and tool-loop usage totals stay consistent end-to-end.** `ChatPanel.tsx` now treats `run-*` handoff sockets as retryable streams, keeps the last assistant bubble in streaming mode while run events are still arriving, and preserves the loading placeholder until real assistant text appears even if tool cards already rendered. `app.py` also requeues the in-flight event on generic websocket send failures, and `chat_manager.py` now emits normalized usage dicts with both `prompt/completion` and `prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens` aliases so UI counters, cost estimation, and concierge telemetry agree. Added regressions in `tests/test_chat_manager_usage.py` and `editor/src/lib/__tests__/chatStreamLifecycle.test.ts`.
- [feat] **Repeated reads of the same file now collapse into one tool card with an open-file link.** The chat UI now groups same-turn `file_read` calls by path, merges their line-range summaries, and renders a single file-focused card instead of showing one nearly identical card per range. Added a small Electron shell bridge so the expanded card can open the referenced local file directly from the desktop app.
- [fix] **Long tool-heavy chat runs now survive transient socket drops better and avoid repeated file artifacts.** Recent log review showed the latest “suspension” runs were no longer pure LLM stalls: the server kept progressing through tool turns, but the live chat WebSocket closed mid-run, which left the last saved assistant message stuck on a progress placeholder. Fixed by letting `/api/chat/{channel}/events` keep the producer/queue alive across unexpected disconnects and teaching `ChatPanel.tsx` to retry the same stream channel a couple of times before surfacing a failure. Also reduced noisy repetition during long research turns: `send_message_with_tools()` now reuses cached capability results for exact duplicate calls plus already-covered `file_read` ranges, and attachment chips are deduped by path on both the server stream and the client message state. Added regression coverage for cached repeated `file_read` calls in `tests/test_server/test_multi_turn_tools.py`.
- [fix] **Provider timeouts now harden the broader app, not just this chat loop.** The suspension bug first surfaced in the chat tool loop, but many other DAN code paths also call `provider.complete()` directly. Added shared timeout resolution in `src/dan/providers/__init__.py` (`config.extra.timeout_seconds` → `DAN_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT` → `DAN_LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT`) and wired the OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google chat providers to honor it by default. OpenAI/Anthropic now pass request-level/client-level timeouts, and Google wraps both `complete()` and streamed generation in asyncio timeouts. Added regressions in `tests/test_provider_timeouts.py`.
- [fix] **Chat titles no longer open with raw filesystem paths or conversational filler in the active header.** Draft thread titles now strip path-heavy prompt noise (`/Users/...`, `can you`, `in this folder`, `help me write`) before the first turn is rendered, and the editor does an early best-effort refresh against the server-authored thread title so the active header can switch from the cleaned draft title to the real generated/fallback title during the first streamed response instead of waiting for the turn to finish.
- [fix] **Chat first-turn titles and mid-stream history persistence are now much more reliable.** The editor now persists the initial user+assistant turn as soon as the stream is accepted, so server-side auto-title generation can start immediately instead of waiting for a terminal event. Streaming state is also saved incrementally: token/run snapshots are debounced, tool/file/run milestones are persisted as they arrive, disconnect/error paths flush pending snapshots, and the chat thread update endpoint no longer re-saves stale thread snapshots that could overwrite fresher titles/messages. Title-generation failures are now retryable on later saves instead of permanently pinning a thread to its fallback title.
- [fix] **Complex path-scoped research/writing requests now use agent-mode tools without workflow mutation.** `DirectTaskHandler` had hardcoded `mode="conversation"` for all direct-task fallbacks, which gave the LLM fewer tool capabilities and a weaker prompt for large report-generation asks. Added `_looks_like_complex_direct_task()` in `classifier.py` and made `DirectTaskHandler` promote matching requests into `agent` mode with `allow_mutation_tool=False`, so they get the fuller tool set without ever proposing graph mutations. The concierge non-build fast path is preserved (skipping the heavy solver is critical — the solver/intent-compiler takes 600+ seconds for these prompts). Added regressions in `tests/test_server/test_direct_task_complexity.py`.
- [fix] **Chat no longer hangs indefinitely when the LLM API stalls after tool execution.** The tool-loop follow-up `provider.complete()` call had no wall-clock timeout — if the API hung (common with custom endpoints like kimi-k2.5), the entire pipeline blocked silently, the heartbeat loop couldn't emit progress events, and the WS consumer eventually disconnected without producing any output. Fixed by adding a configurable `DAN_LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT` (default 120s) plus a shared guarded-completion path inside `send_message_with_tools()`, so the initial call, continuation, follow-up, retry/replan, and synthesis completions all inherit timeout/cancellation handling and can still emit periodic `progress_ack` events while waiting. Also fixed leaked `_produce()` tasks: when the WS consumer disconnects, the orphaned producer task is now cancelled instead of hanging forever.
- [fix] **False stale-graph warnings no longer trigger just because the editor loaded an auto-laid-out graph.** The editor was computing `client_graph_revision` from the `layout=true` graph payload used for rendering, while the server compared chat requests against the persisted graph revision. That meant `Graph changed since your last message` could appear on long-running chats even when nothing meaningful changed. Fixed by returning canonical `graph_revision` values from the graph load/save APIs, storing that revision in `editor/src/store/useGraphStore.ts`, and teaching `ChatPanel.tsx` to prefer the server-authored revision for clean graphs but fall back to a local canonical hash when the current graph has unsaved local edits. Added regressions in `tests/test_server/test_chat_integration.py` and `editor/src/lib/__tests__/chatGraphRevision.test.ts`.
- [fix] **Chat tool-loop budgets now scale much better with newer large-context model families.** The first output-budget patch stopped hangs, but it still treated modern 200K/1M-class models too conservatively and under-recognized newer model names like `claude-opus-4.6`, `gpt5.4`, `MiniMax-M2.5-highspeed`, `glm5`, and `kimi-k2.5`. Updated `src/dan/server/chat_manager.py` so `_get_context_window()` normalizes model aliases and recognizes newer families, and `_completion_max_tokens()` now uses more generous soft tiers (32K / 48K / 64K depending on effective context window) instead of a flat ~16K cap. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_server/test_chat_manager.py` and updated `tests/test_server/test_multi_turn_tools.py`.
- [fix] **33-10 final code-review patches: composed compilation wiring, orphaned subgraphs, JSON extraction.** Addressed edge cases found in final review. (1) `IntentCompiler._compile_segment` and `_build_segment` now correctly track the *first* entry node when falling back to individual stage compilation, preventing upstream nodes from being wired incorrectly into the *exit* of the segment (e.g. bypassing a conditional gate). (2) `unwrap_loop` macro in `structural_mutations.py` now recursively deletes associated `body_graph`, `then_graph`, `else_graph`, and `sub_graph` references to prevent orphaned subgraphs in the JSON payload. (3) `_parse_scores` in `tests/eval/judge.py` now uses `text.find("{")` and `text.rfind("}")` instead of a fragile regex that failed on nested braces. (4) `parallelize` macro now appends a truncation warning to `MutationMacroResult.error` instead of silently dropping nodes beyond the limit of 5. (5) `_negate_condition_ast` explicitly handles `ast.Name`.
- [fix] **Restored bounded tool-loop output budgets and made `dan-up` persistent logs capture DAN app diagnostics.** The live `send_message_with_tools()` path still omitted `max_tokens` on initial/follow-up/continuation/synthesis completions, so long post-tool generations could hang or starve the model of output budget despite the earlier reliability pass. Fixed by adding a shared `_completion_max_tokens()` budget helper and passing it through the multi-turn tool loop (including retry/replan branches). Also updated the uvicorn startup config used by `dan-serve` and `dan-service-runner` so `dan.*` loggers emit at `INFO`, which means `dan-up`'s existing `~/.dan/logs/server.log` now captures `chat_manager` tool-loop diagnostics instead of only uvicorn process lines. Added regressions in `tests/test_server/test_multi_turn_tools.py` and `tests/test_server/test_server_logging.py`.
- [fix] **33-10 follow-up hardening: conservative tool inference and whole-condition review negation.** `_infer_tool_id()` now uses longest-first word-boundary matching and drops the generic `file` catch-all, avoiding false positives like `profile customer behavior` → `file_read`. `_normalize_review_condition()` now masks/restores string literals safely, negates stop-conditions via AST across compound `and`/`or` expressions, falls back to the safe default on malformed stop-conditions, and recognizes reversed threshold forms like `8 <= quality_score`. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_meta/test_review_condition_normalization.py`; verification: `pytest tests/test_meta/test_review_condition_normalization.py tests/test_eval_semantic_patch.py` (`28` passing).
- [fix] **Chat thread persistence now round-trips tool traces, run events, cost/scoped-run metadata, and file attachments.** The editor already serialized `tool_calls`, `run_events`, `estimated_cost`, scoped `run_ref`, and attachment chips, but `ChatStore` and the frontend save/load mapper silently dropped parts of that metadata so reloaded threads lost execution context and artifact links. Fixed by persisting metadata fields in `src/dan/server/chat_store.py`, extracting a shared `editor/src/lib/chatMessagePersistence.ts` mapper used by `ChatPanel`, restoring `estimated_cost` + scoped `run_ref` target fields, and hardening timestamp/tool-call fallback handling. Added regression coverage in both `tests/test_server/test_chat_store.py` and `editor/src/lib/__tests__/chatMessagePersistence.test.ts`.
- [fix] **33-10 code-review follow-up: restored live source changes, tightened expectation gate specificity, and unified live tool catalogs.** Follow-up review caught 3 important gaps after the first 33-10 pass. (1) Review-condition normalization now ignores quoted string literals, preserves valid Python expressions like `is not None` / `in (...)`, and uses a shared JSON-safe placeholder-code helper so direct-build code stubs stay syntactically valid even with quotes/newlines. (2) The eval expectation gate now reads real DAN graph schema more precisely: `GraphSummary` tracks `has_review_loop`, `review_loop_count`, `has_conditional`, `has_parallel_subagents`, and `has_merge`, unified `gate` nodes are classified by `config.gate_mode` (`while` vs `if_else`), and `nested_review_loops` now requires at least two review loops. (3) Tool-awareness now uses a shared live registry-backed helper `src/dan/meta/tool_catalog.py` for both codegen and intent extraction prompts, removing the earlier hardcoded 17-vs-19 tool-list divergence and aligning the codegen catalog with `text_chunk` examples. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_meta/test_review_condition_normalization.py` (10 passing) and `tests/test_eval_semantic_patch.py` (10 passing), including structural-mutation review-loop wiring coverage.
- [fix] **Tool loop architecture: finish_reason tracking, dynamic compaction, truncation continuation.** Three structural fixes to the multi-turn tool loop: (1) `CompletionResult` gains `finish_reason` field, captured in all providers (OpenAI `choices[0].finish_reason`, Anthropic `stop_reason`, Google `candidates[0].finish_reason`). (2) `_compact_context()` dynamically manages context before every LLM call — 3-pass strategy: first truncates tool results (oldest first, 1500→500→200 chars), then summarizes old assistant messages to first+last sentence, then drops oldest turns keeping system + last 6. (3) When `finish_reason` is `length`/`max_tokens` (output truncated), the loop automatically injects a continuation prompt instead of treating the truncated response as final. (4) Diagnostic logging after every LLM call: `finish_reason`, `has_text`, `has_tools`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `context_msgs`. (5) System prompt now instructs models to use `file_write` with append mode for long outputs and `file_read` with grep for large files.
- [feat] **Tool efficiency: search+fetch combo, extract-only fetch, richer directory listing.** (1) `web_search` gains `num_results` (1-10, default 3) and `fetch_content` (auto-fetches+cleans the top result inline — saves a whole LLM turn). (2) `web_fetch` gains `extract_only` keyword parameter — greps the fetched page and returns only matching lines with context instead of the full page. (3) `list_directory` now shows modification dates (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`) and relative paths for recursive listings, so the LLM can pick recent/relevant files without extra `file_read` calls. (4) Review fixes: `file_grep` regex compile wrapped in try/except (falls back to escaped literal), overlapping context ranges merged, `_has_filesystem_path` strips URLs before matching, `_clean_tool_result` covers `file_grep`, heartbeat task properly cancelled on generator teardown, synthesis call at max turns doesn't waste tokens on tool definitions, `Math.max` guarded against empty array.
- [feat] **Smart file reading: line ranges, inline grep, and `file_grep` tool.** Upgraded `file_read` with `start_line`/`end_line` for reading specific line ranges and `grep` parameter for keyword search with 2-line context — so the LLM can find relevant sections before loading entire files. Added `file_grep` tool for searching across files in a directory with glob filtering. Returns matching lines with filenames, line numbers, and context. Both tools report `total_lines` in result data so the LLM knows the file size. The LLM can now: (1) `file_grep` to find where a keyword appears across a codebase, (2) `file_read` with `grep` to search within a single file, (3) `file_read` with `start_line`/`end_line` to read just the relevant section. This avoids loading entire 100KB files into context when only a few lines matter.
- [fix] **Tool result cleaning: strip markup boilerplate before feeding back to LLM.** Added `_clean_tool_result()` in `chat_manager.py` that strips content-free markup before tool results enter the LLM context. `web_fetch`/`web_search` results: HTML tags, `<script>`/`<style>`/`<nav>`/`<footer>` blocks, image markdown, bare image URLs, and dense navigation link blocks removed. `file_read` results: LaTeX preambles (`\\documentclass`, `\\usepackage`, `\\begin{document}`) and boilerplate commands stripped while preserving `\\section`/content; HTML files get full tag stripping. Plain text and data results pass through verbatim. Applied at the tool-result-message construction point (replaces raw `[:4000]` truncation with clean + truncate).
- [fix] **Follow-up LLM call after tool execution: context compaction.** After 10 tool calls with 4000-char results each, messages could be 40K+ tokens, leaving almost no room for the model's output — causing it to either return empty, repeat tool calls, or get cut off mid-generation. Fixed by compacting tool result messages to 1500 chars each when estimated input exceeds 60% of context window. Also fixed `ToolCallGroup` duration display: was summing individual tool times (showing 7.3s for parallel tools), now shows `Math.max()` wall-clock time (~2s).
- [fix] **Chat flow audit: 10 patches across server + UI.** Comprehensive review of the message→classification→handler→LLM→stream→render pipeline. Fixes: (1) **Suspended response after tool calls:** follow-up LLM call had no heartbeat — added 25s heartbeat wrapper with `progress_ack` keepalive, matching the codegen path pattern. (2) **Empty assistant bubble:** added fallback content when LLM returns nothing after tool execution. (3) **WS keepalive:** `chat_events_ws` now sends `{"type":"ping"}` every 25s of silence to prevent proxy/browser timeout disconnects. (4) **Graph not refreshing:** ChatPanel now handles `chat_graph_created` events and calls `loadGraph()`. (5) **Validation errors silently swallowed:** ChatPanel now handles `chat_validation_result` and shows error toast. (6) **File attachments invisible:** ChatPanel now handles `chat_file_attachment` and appends file info to message content. (7) **HandlerRegistry KeyError crash:** `get()` now falls back to CONVERSATION handler instead of crashing. (8) **Opaque dispatcher errors:** all 3 dispatcher catch blocks now include `type(exc).__name__` in the user-facing message. (9) **Silent tool-calling degradation:** fallback to text-only stream now logged at WARNING instead of DEBUG. (10) **Max tool turns raw dump:** forces a `tool_choice="none"` synthesis call when the loop ends with tool-only output. ChatPanel also handles `ping` events as no-ops.
- [fix] **WhatsApp Web `allowed_jids` is now exact and outbound-enforced.** The live-smoke safety control already existed, but it only filtered inbound messages by sender substring, so a guarded run could still send to another chat and allowed-sender messages from group chats leaked through. The adapter now: (1) canonicalizes bare numbers / JIDs with `:device` suffix stripping for `s.whatsapp.net` only, (2) rejects cross-server matches (`@lid`, `@g.us` no longer match phone-number allowlist entries), (3) guards inbound on `chat_jid` before media download instead of `sender_jid` after processing, (4) blocks disallowed text/file/fallback sends before recipient resolution. Verification: `tests/test_adapters/test_whatsapp_web.py` (`27`) + `tests/test_cli_whatsapp_messaging.py` (`15`) = `42` passing.

All tagged `practical` for `--tag practical` filtering. Also added `--tag` CLI flag to eval harness for tag-based prompt filtering. Documented in 33-4 and eval-run-guide with overnight run command.

- [docs] **33-10 plan: Semantic Correctness Patch.** Created `docs/plans/33-10-semantic-correctness-patch.md` — 6 focused patches to fix contract bugs and eval blind spots found by LLM-as-judge review of all stored eval graphs. (A) Review-loop condition polarity mismatch: `ReviewRequirement.condition` defaults to `"quality_score >= 8"` (stop condition) but `Builder.review_loop()` interprets it as continue-while — loops run backwards. (B) Eval pass/fail ignores fixture expectations (`min_nodes`, `topology`, `node_types`): any valid graph passes, inflating reported rates. (C) Tool nodes default to `web_search` / code nodes default to `result = 'done'` — add keyword inference and descriptive placeholders. (D) Codegen prompt has no tool catalog — inject registered tool IDs. (E) LLM-as-judge scoring via `--judge` flag. (F) Intent extraction tool-awareness. Implementation order: A+B in parallel (highest ROI), then C+D+F (generation quality), then E (diagnostic).
- [fix] **Tool-use responses now show planning text and don't stop silently.** Two issues with the multi-turn tool-call loop in `send_message_with_tools()`: (1) when the LLM produced text alongside tool calls (e.g. "Now let me search for..."), that text was only appended to the message history for the next LLM call but never emitted to the UI as a `ChatTokenEvent`, so the user saw tool calls starting with no context; (2) when the follow-up LLM call after tool execution returned empty text, the `ChatCompleteEvent` had empty content that overwrote any previously shown text. Fixed by emitting a `ChatTokenEvent` with the LLM's planning text before executing tool calls, falling back to accumulated tool results when the follow-up response is empty, and using `||` instead of `??` in the ChatPanel content update so empty final events don't wipe out existing content.
- [fix] **Smarter path-scoped task detection in classifier.** Messages containing filesystem paths (e.g. "help me write a supply chain report in tex" with an embedded `/path/to/dir`) were misrouted to `FILE_REQUEST` file-search instead of the tool-using `DIRECT_TASK` handler. Replaced narrow `_looks_like_path_write_request` with `_looks_like_path_scoped_task` that uses 6 signal categories: help-me+action verbs, format specifiers ("in tex/latex/markdown"), multi-action instructions ("download and cite"), creative verb+output noun pairs, retrieval-verb start exclusion, and path-stripped verb detection (prevents "draft" in `draft.pdf` from counting as a creative verb). Lowered `has_path` fallback confidence from 0.9 to 0.65 so the LLM classifier can override for ambiguous cases. 34 regression tests in `tests/test_server/test_classifier_path.py`.

Flakiness rate 60%→30% (halved). Granular failure categories decompose 97.5% of failures: timeout_planning=29 (72%), stream_error=7 (18%), misrouted=3 (8%), no_graph_created=1 (2%). Generation summary event captured on passed builds: intent_compiler=55%, codegen=5%, unknown=40%. Quality avg 94.3. Node range calibration applied (T1→2-5, T2→3-8). T5 median latency 58s (above 15s target — classifier confidence <0.7 on some prompts). Path distribution and T5 latency sections now in eval report.

- [feat] **Chat titles are now explicitly user-editable in the UI.** The chat panel already supported title updates at the API level, but renaming was hidden behind a click-on-text affordance. `ChatPanel.tsx` now exposes visible rename controls: a pencil action beside the active thread title and a rename action on each history row with inline editing. Manual edits normalize whitespace, update the active header immediately, and flow through the server-side title lock so auto-generated titles never overwrite user intent. Added `editor/src/lib/chatThreadTitle.ts` plus `chatThreadTitle.test.ts`.
- [feat] **Chat threads now auto-generate titles from the first user message.** Added `src/dan/server/chat_titles.py` to produce compact thread/tab titles with the cheapest available model (`micro` tier, with safe fallback to the configured chat model or prompt truncation). The server now marks UI-provided draft titles as replaceable fallbacks, generates a better title asynchronously after the first user turn is saved, and protects manual renames from being overwritten. The desktop/editor chat refreshes thread summaries after terminal events and when history opens so generated titles show up in the sidebar and active header.
- [fix] **Editor chat now follows queued stream handoffs.** `ChatPanel.tsx` did not handle `chat_queued`, so when the concierge dispatcher redirected a request onto a replacement stream channel the desktop/full-screen chat stayed on the original socket and the assistant bubble remained empty. The renderer now updates the placeholder bubble with a queue message, follows the redirected `stream_channel_id`, and continues streaming the eventual progress/final response. `ChatStreamEvent` in `editor/src/types/chat.ts` now models `chat_queued` metadata as well.
- [fix] **UI chat follow-up fixes: Enter send, compact tool-call groups, and non-terminal progress updates.** Tightened the desktop/full-screen chat experience after live use. `ChatPanel.tsx` now sends Enter presses using the textarea's live value (avoids stale-state misses), and treats `chat_complete` events with `detected_mode="progress_ack"` as interim status instead of final completion so the WebSocket stays open until the real answer arrives. `ChatMessage.tsx` now keeps tool-call groups collapsed by default and surfaces the latest running tool in the collapsed summary line.

- [docs] **32-7 direct execution architecture plan.** Created `docs/plans/32-7-direct-execution-architecture.md` — comprehensive plan for eliminating the codegen→sandbox→validate roundtrip for complex tasks. Core idea: `IntentCompiler.build_graph()` constructs Graph objects directly in-process by calling the builder API, then hands them to `Engine.run()`. Concierge gets an inline execution path for natural-language complex tasks (default) while explicit workflow-build requests keep the existing build-session/codegen path. Post-hoc `graph_to_builder_code()` materializes scripts for reuse/documentation after execution. 9 task groups: in-process graph construction, planner direct-build path, concierge inline execution, routing logic, post-hoc materialization, telemetry, error handling/fallback, configuration, documentation. - [fix] **Concierge simple-turn fast path + surface-owned Telegram identity.** Added a conservative fast path in `runtime.py` for short social turns and simple `direct_task` asks (short drafting + direct live lookups), so they skip memory/domain/artifact prep when there are no pending follow-ups, active goals, attachments, or explicit build/plan/debug modes. During verification, a real edge case turned up: single-word acknowledgement replies like `yes` / `ok` / `sure` still matched the broad greeting token set, so they could slip into the fast path. Fixed by explicitly excluding short reply-ack tokens from fast-path eligibility. Telegram fleet no longer injects a competing per-bot system message into `history`; it now sends structured `surface_context` metadata (`identity` + `peers`), and concierge handlers render that metadata as extra system instructions. Added/extended regression coverage in `tests/test_concierge/test_runtime_fast_path.py`, `tests/test_concierge/test_handlers.py`, `tests/test_server/test_chat_manager.py`, and `tests/test_adapters/test_telegram_fleet.py`; focused suites now pass (`111` tests).

Each `RoutingSignal` evaluates independently and the first non-None result wins. Default chain: `MentionSignal` (1.0) → `ReplyOwnershipSignal` (0.9) → `TopicMappingSignal` (0.85) → `ProjectKeywordSignal` (0.7) → `DefaultBotSignal` (0.1). The new `ReplyOwnershipSignal` fixes the "wrong bot takeover" problem: replying to scholar's message now routes to scholar, not the default bot. Fleet wires `_lookup_reply_to_bot()` (extracts bot name from `_message_lanes` lane keys) into the route call. Signals are configurable via `add_signal()`, `remove_signal()`, `set_signals()`. 27 router tests + 5 new fleet tests, all 101 adapter tests pass.

(2) Concierge classification now treats raw filesystem paths as a fallback signal instead of an unconditional win: stronger intent cues (meta-goal/workflow) run first, true path-scoped create/write requests (for example "create a new project folder under Dropbox/...") route to `direct_task`, and plain read/review requests with paths still route to `file_request`. Added 6 classifier regressions and 2 Telegram adapter regressions.

(6) Eval harness: runner uses `source` from `chat_code_generated` for generation_path; report shows intent compiler activation rate per tier (Activation % column). 2 new tests for JSON-in-content extraction; `test_fully_covered_intent_uses_sandbox_execution` renamed to `test_fully_covered_intent_uses_in_process_execution`.
- [fix] **Live factual queries routed to conversation mode.** `detect_chat_mode()` previously sent all questions (including "What happened for ONDAS...") to `ask` mode, where the model often produced text-only responses without calling `web_search`. Added a heuristic: messages containing live-data phrases (what happened, recent, news, milestone, latest, today, updates, headlines, etc.) now route to `conversation` mode so tools are available. Regression test: `test_live_market_news_query_uses_conversation_mode`.

Found 4 gaps: (1) no pre-sandbox `ast.parse()` syntax check — syntax errors go to subprocess and silently fail with no diagnosis, (2) sandbox returns `None` → `codegen_errors = []` → diagnosis loop guard skips it entirely, (3) post-diagnosis re-validation is hardcoded `success=True` (not actual validation), (4) post-mutation validation is skipped — `save_graph()` called directly after `dispatch_compound_mutations()` without `validate_graph()`. Added tasks 9-12 to 33-8 and tasks 2-5/2-6 to 33-7. Added companion step chain diagram to parent plan (33-generation-quality-eval.md). Principle: no step should have a "silent None" exit.
- [docs] **Phase 33 patch subplans (33-6, 33-7, 33-8) — post-pilot improvement plans.** Three parallel subplans addressing the top improvement areas from the Phase 33 pilot findings. **33-6 Intent Compiler Activation:** debug and fix 0% intent compiler activation — intent extraction, coverage matching, and provider tool-call support. **33-7 Semantic Quality Gates:** catch underspecified graphs (p02: 2-node review loop, p08: 1-node equity research) with node count, pattern presence, tool coverage, and topology checks; quality scoring (0-100) with optional threshold rejection. **33-8 Codegen Resilience & Provider Hardening:** LLM retry/fallback for codegen and intent extraction, classifier empty-response fallback to heuristic, WebSocket keepalive hardening, granular failure categories (split `no_graph_created` into 7 subcategories), multi-run stability measurement (`--runs N` with flakiness detection). All three are parallelizable and informed by 33-5 findings. Updated parent plan, dependency graph, success criteria, todo.md.
- [fix] **Concierge CONFIRM bypass + META_GOAL classification override for explicit build mode.** Two interacting bugs blocked 2/4 failing eval prompts. (1) `resolve_policy()` returned `ActionPolicy.CONFIRM` for `META_GOAL` intents (estimated cost 2.0 > threshold 1.0), and the CONFIRM handler at line 1979 returned early BEFORE the solver-path bypass at line 2036 — so `_requested_mode_forces_solver_path()` never had a chance to run. Fixed by adding `not _requested_mode_forces_solver_path(msg.metadata)` to the CONFIRM guard. (2) Classification override only caught `CONVERSATION` → `WORKFLOW_BUILD`, but complex prompts like "Build a multi-department research system" were classified as `META_GOAL`, bypassing the override. Extended to also catch `META_GOAL` when `requested_mode` is "build" or "mutate".
- [fix] **Eval runner: scan all events for clarification signals.** The runner only checked `response_text` for clarification patterns, but the server's "Please confirm" messages were tagged as `progress_ack` events (continued by the stream consumer), so `response_text` ended up as "Meta session started" which didn't match any signal. Added `_any_event_needs_clarification()` to scan all event contents. Also added "meta session started" to `_CLARIFICATION_SIGNALS` with auto-reply "yes, proceed".
- [test] **4 new regression tests for clarification scanning.** `test_meta_session_detected_as_clarification`, `test_any_event_needs_clarification_scans_all_events`, `test_any_event_needs_clarification_returns_none_when_clean`, `test_follow_up_helpers_handle_confirmation_prompt` (existing, extended). 6 total eval+concierge tests pass.
- [fix] **`SurfaceMessage.surface_id` AttributeError crash in concierge runtime.** `process()` referenced `msg.surface_id` at the notification broadcast (line 1450) but `SurfaceMessage` only has `surface` and `external_id`. Crash killed all message processing after the initial progressive feedback — the final response was never sent. Fixed to `msg.external_id` (notification routing) and `msg.surface` (telemetry recording).
- [feat] **Preflight tool hook system for automatic context injection.** Tools can now declare a `preflight` block in their `TOOL_METADATA` with `trigger` (`"always"` or `"pattern"` with regex list), `format` (template string), `inject_as` (`"system_context"`), and `args` (default kwargs). `ChatManager._run_preflight_hooks()` scans all preflight-enabled tools before building messages and injects formatted results into the system prompt. `current_datetime` uses `trigger: "always"` so the date is always present without an LLM tool call. Replaces the previous hardcoded `datetime.now()` injection. `get_preflight_tools()` added to `dan.tools.__init__` for discovery. Falls back to manual date if preflight fails.

Generation path: 50% codegen, 0% intent_compiler, 50% unknown. Total run 782s. Updated `33-generation-quality-eval.md` (Pilot Findings), `33-1-manual-pilot.md` (completed, tasks checked), `33-3-small-task-battery.md` (pilot subset note), `todo.md` (33-1 completed).
- [fix] **PydanticSerializationError crash in concierge — `asyncio.Event` leaked into `PendingAction` metadata.** `app.py` passes `cancel_event` (an `asyncio.Event`) in `SurfaceMessage.metadata`. When the concierge stored a `PendingAction` with `metadata=dict(msg.metadata)`, `project.model_dump_json()` crashed with `PydanticSerializationError: Unable to serialize unknown type: <class 'asyncio.locks.Event'>`. Fixed by adding `_safe_metadata()` helper in `runtime.py` that strips non-JSON-serializable values before persisting. Applied to all 4 `PendingAction` construction sites. Also added `requested_mode` to `SurfaceMessage.metadata` in `app.py` so the concierge can see the original pre-normalization mode (since `normalize_chat_mode("build")` maps to `"agent"`).
- [fix] **Concierge classification override for explicit build mode.** When `requested_mode` is `"build"` or `"mutate"` and the classifier returns `CONVERSATION` (due to empty LLM response or keyword mismatch), the concierge now overrides to `WORKFLOW_BUILD` with 0.9 confidence. This prevents build-lane prompts from being treated as casual conversation.
- [fix] **Concierge goal-orchestrator bypass for explicit build mode.** Added `_requested_mode_forces_solver_path()` helper. When `requested_mode` is `"build"` or `"mutate"`, the concierge skips the goal orchestrator (Phase 29 path) and goes directly to the solver path. This avoids the multi-turn reuse/confirm/plan-the-broader-goal loop that adds latency and complexity for explicit build requests.
- [fix] **Eval runner stream handling — progress-ack events, wall timeout, clarification auto-reply.** (1) `_consume_stream()` now skips `chat_complete` events with `detected_mode="progress_ack"` and only breaks on final terminal events, preventing premature stream termination on reassurance pings. (2) Added 90s wall-clock timeout to `_consume_stream()` so progress-ack pings don't keep the stream alive indefinitely. (3) Added clarification auto-reply loop in `run_single()` — detects server prompts like "reuse/adapt/start fresh?" and "please confirm" and responds automatically ("3" for start-fresh, "yes" for confirm). (4) Fixed `_validate()` to infer `passed=True` when `errors=[]` (the validate endpoint doesn't return a `valid` field). (5) Events now stored with key fields (message_id, content, detected_mode) instead of just type.
- [test] **Eval runner regression tests.** Added `tests/test_eval_runner.py` with 2 tests: (1) `test_consume_stream_ignores_progress_complete_and_stops_on_final` verifies progress-ack skip + terminal break behavior. (2) `test_follow_up_helpers_handle_confirmation_prompt` verifies clarification detection and auto-reply for confirmation prompts. Added `tests/test_concierge_runtime_modes.py` with 1 test verifying `_requested_mode_forces_solver_path()` for build/mutate/agent modes.
- [fix] **Guard 2 confidence threshold too aggressive — lowered 0.7 → 0.4.** The understanding guard (Check 4) in `entity_grounding.py` fired clarification on any solver decision with confidence < 0.7. Since the heuristic solver path always applies a `-0.1` penalty (e.g., classification at 0.75 → solver at 0.65), the guard caught most normal messages — including clear follow-ups like "can you update?" — producing needless "I'm not fully confident I understood correctly" replies. Lowered threshold to 0.4 so only genuinely unclear inputs trigger clarification. Updated test to use confidence 0.3 (below new threshold).
- [fix] **Current date not available to LLM — injected into system prompt.** The system prompt told the LLM to "call `current_datetime` tool" to learn the date, but the LLM frequently skipped that tool call and jumped straight to `web_search`, meaning it had no idea what "recent" meant relative to today. Fixed by injecting `**Today is {current_date}.**` directly into `UNIFIED_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (resolved at message-build time via `datetime.now()`). Updated rules to reflect the date is now always available. The `current_datetime` tool remains for exact time/timezone queries.
- [fix] **Infinite clarification loop in concierge response pipeline.** Two interacting bugs caused the bot to repeat "Before I proceed: I'm making some assumptions..." indefinitely regardless of user replies. Bug 1: `_heuristic_decision()` in `solver.py` populated `assumptions=["Inferred from classification heuristic without LLM planning"]` — a system-internal diagnostic note whose content words never overlap with any normal user message, so `guard_understanding()` in `entity_grounding.py` always flagged it as "ungrounded" and emitted a clarification. Bug 2: When the user answered the clarification, the replay message re-entered `_solver_path()` with no guard bypass, producing the same ungrounded assumption and the same clarification question — an infinite loop with no exit. Fixed by (1) removing the system-internal assumption from heuristic decisions (`assumptions=[]`), and (2) adding `clarification_answer` / `clarification_auto_note` checks to skip Guard 1 and Guard 2 on clarification replay messages (matching the existing skip pattern used for Guard 3 / completion guard). Updated 3 solver tests that asserted the removed heuristic assumption text. 1342 concierge tests pass.

- [docs] **Plan 31-19: Request Guard Pipeline.** Created detailed subplan for inter-step guards, entity awareness, and system-prompt clarification rules. Addresses architectural gap where the concierge pipeline (classify → resolve → execute → post-process) has no validation between steps — the LLM acts on wrong assumptions instead of asking for clarification. Design based on industry survey of DeerFlow 2.0, OpenClaw, CrewAI (task guardrails), Google ADK (6-point callbacks), LangGraph (Reflexion), AutoGen (nested chat), and Anthropic (think tool). Six task groups: entity grounding, Guard 1 (classification coherence), Guard 2 (understanding coherence), Guard 3 (response relevance), system prompt updates, loop composition.

Partial name matching supported. Registered in command registry with subcommand descriptors. Removed context-based project-status heuristic from classifier — "any updates on the kaggle project" no longer triggers `STATUS_CHECK` or causes file sends. Cleaned up `_looks_like_topical_status_request`, `_DAN_PROJECT_CONTEXT`, `_EXTERNAL_TOPIC_NOUNS`, `_PROJECT_STATUS_WORDS` constants. 15 new tests, all classifier tests updated.
- [feat] **Project-scoped memory (31-18).** Memories stored during a project conversation are now automatically tagged with the project's ID and scoped to `PROJECT`. Retrieval filters out other projects' `PROJECT`-scoped items while keeping `USER`/`GLOBAL` items visible everywhere. This means project-specific facts (file paths, data locations), preferences (citation style, formatting rules), and principles (domain constraints) stay isolated to their project — like workspace-level rules that activate by context. `MemoryKernel.retrieve()` and `retrieve_by_task()` gain an optional `project_id` parameter; matching project items get a 0.3 score bonus. `store_fact()`, `store_preference()`, `store_principle()` gain optional `project_id` — sets `scope=PROJECT` and `metadata["project_id"]` automatically. All concierge store paths (`_store_memory_candidates`, `_try_extract_preferences`, `_try_memory_extraction`, correction-driven stores) thread the active `project_id`. After context resolution, a supplementary project-scoped query enriches memory context. 19 new tests, 3 pre-existing test fixes. Zero regressions (1339 concierge tests pass).
- [feat] **Telegram project tracing.** Telegram replies now show a compact `[ProjectName]` header at the top of each message (converted from the concierge's `[DAN - Project]` prefix), combined with Telegram's native `reply_to_message_id` for conversational threading. The `_format_for_telegram()` function replaces `_strip_prefix_and_html()` — it extracts the project/task label and reformats it as `[Project]\n...` instead of stripping entirely. `identity.py` gains `extract_label_from_prefix()` and `format_compact_label()` helpers. `_format_reply_label()` in runtime now always includes the project label for all surfaces (previously only when multiple projects existed). 5 new adapter tests, 8 new identity tests.

Backoff factor configurable via `DAN_TELEGRAM_PROGRESS_BACKOFF` (default 1.5). If other messages have been sent in the chat since the last progress edit (conversation has moved on), the adapter sends a new reply instead of editing the stale message. Separate `progress_msg_id` tracking prevents progress edits from corrupting the content message.

## 2026-03-10
- [refactor] Moved content-quality rules from per-surface `SURFACE_HINTS` into the core `UNIFIED_SYSTEM_PROMPT` rules (rules 7-8). "Never dump raw tool output", "never include image markdown / nav blocks / raw HTML" now apply to **all surfaces** (Telegram, WhatsApp, CLI, Editor) from the core layer. Surface hints now contain only formatting guidance (markdown dialect, code block support, HTML restrictions). This follows the project architecture principle that the concierge/core layer handles content quality regardless of frontend. `_sanitize_web_content()` in `capability_handlers.py` remains as the first-pass tool-result sanitizer; the core prompt rules are the second-pass LLM-level guardrail.
- [fix] `FileHandler._candidate_search_dirs()` now scopes file searches to the active conversation context instead of falling back to broad `~/Dropbox` search. It scans assistant turns (not just user turns) for path references, and checks the project summary for directory hints. Previously, vague follow-up messages like "the first folder, please review" with no explicit path fell through to searching all of `~/Dropbox`, `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, producing irrelevant matches from unrelated directories.
- [fix] Review follow-up for 31-14: messaging-surface `ProgressSession`s are now cleaned up even on the concierge's messaging fast path, phase-event throttling is tracked per `ProgressSession` instead of globally, and Telegram attachment-/poll-only replies replace any visible progress bubble with a terminal delivery outcome. Confirmed non-text deliveries now emit status text like `Delivered the requested file.` / `Sent the requested poll.`, while failed poll/file sends fall back to an explicit terminal error instead of leaving stale progress text or falsely claiming success. This closes the remaining cross-surface interference and stale-progress UX bugs from the adapter-owned progress refactor.
- [refactor] **Progress ownership moved from concierge to adapter layer for messaging surfaces.** The concierge reassurance timer (timeout-based "Working on it..." bubbles) is now disabled for telegram/whatsapp/email. Those surfaces own their own progress UX: the Telegram fleet's `_stream_with_edits` has a drain-queue pattern with its own timer (10s initial / 20s repeat, configurable via `DAN_TELEGRAM_PROGRESS_DELAY` / `DAN_TELEGRAM_PROGRESS_INTERVAL`). Fast replies ("Hi") never show a progress bubble. Queue wait hints from `_iter_chat_stream_events` include elapsed time and queue position. CLI/editor still uses the concierge timer since those surfaces lack an adapter-level renderer. Queue key is `project_id` (same-project serial, different-project concurrent); `task_id` stays contextual — intra-project parallelism is possible by extending the key later without restructuring the dispatcher. Concierge `_make_phase_event` progress_ack events are silently dropped for messaging surfaces so the adapter is the single source of progress UX.
- [fix] Telegram fleet now follows dispatcher `chat_queued` stream redirects instead of waiting on the original dead channel. Same-project messages sent in quick succession can be queued behind an earlier turn; `/api/chat/message` signals that by emitting `chat_queued` with a replacement `stream_channel_id`. The fleet's direct WebSocket client was ignoring that handoff, so users could see "Working on it..." and then never get the actual answer. Added `_iter_chat_stream_events()` to follow redirected queued channels in both `_stream_with_edits()` and `_stream_collect()`, plus regressions for both paths.
- [fix] File requests with explicit path references now treat the path as search scope, not as part of the literal search query. `FileHandler` was correctly narrowing `search_dirs` when a message mentioned a real directory, but it still passed the raw sentence including the filesystem path into `search_local_files()`, which produced noisy irrelevant matches and "Which file?" clarifications. It now strips explicit paths from the ranking query during scoped searches and labels unique directory hits as `Found folder: ...`.
- [fix] Progressive response phase transitions now emit live events to the stream. Previously `_set_progress_phase` only updated internal `ProgressSession` state, so Telegram users never saw phase-specific messages like "Working on it — Searching files…" or "Still working — Generating response…". Now `_make_phase_event` yields `progress_ack` events at each phase boundary (context, execution), throttled to 1/second. The `process()` wrapper gates these: phase events are suppressed until the reassurance delay (5s) fires, so quick replies still show no interim bubble. After the delay, the first reassurance reads the current phase info, and subsequent phase transitions edit the same Telegram message in place with the latest status.
- [fix] Progress acknowledgments ("Working on it...") now only appear after the reassurance delay (default 5s), not instantly for every message. Quick replies (Hi, Hello, simple questions) that complete within the delay window never show an interim bubble. Previously, Telegram's `compact` verbosity caused an immediate `progress_ack` before the LLM even started, producing a visible "Working on it..." for every message including trivial greetings. The existing `process()` reassurance timer now handles both the initial and repeated progress messages, all marked as `progress_ack` so stream consumers know they're non-terminal.
- [fix] Messaging progress acknowledgments no longer masquerade as final answers. `progress_ack` is still carried on `ChatCompleteEvent` for backward compatibility, but stream consumers now treat `detected_mode="progress_ack"` as non-terminal and keep listening for the real answer. Fixed the shared adapter stream merger, Telegram fleet non-streaming collector, `dan-chat` stream client, and the adapter bridge in `app.py`. Also changed Telegram/other messaging instant acks from echo-style `"Got it. <your request>"` to a generic `"Working on it..."` so the intermediate reply is less awkward while the real answer is still pending.
- [fix] Telegram fleet no longer serializes every private-DM message for a bot behind one adapter-side history lock. Reviewed the working WhatsApp Web path and matched its key property: no adapter-wide execution lock around the full request lifecycle. Telegram now keeps the broader conversation key for server-side continuity, but uses reply-aware local lanes for fleet history/locking (`reply_to_message_id` reuses a lane; unrelated private messages get independent lanes). Added regressions proving unrelated private-DM turns can start in parallel while reply chains stay coherent.
- [refactor] Extracted `DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL` constant in `dan.rag` — all 8 hardcoded `"text-embedding-3-small"` literals across `rag/__init__.py`, `engine/executor.py`, `executors/rag.py`, `server/app.py`, and `server/chat_factory.py` now reference the single constant.
