Wired into `app.py` startup, `DiscoveryService`, command registry, and concierge fast dispatch. `DAN_PROJECT_SKILLS_DIR` env var for project-level override. 48 tests in `tests/test_server/test_skill_store.py` covering frontmatter parsing, IDE compatibility (Cursor/Claude/Codex formats), scanning, importing, Hyperedge conversion, SKILL_LIBRARY population, lookup, scope filtering, and command handling.
- [fix] **Messaging adapters no longer lose queued concierge replies, and long-wait feedback is now phase-aware.** Fixed a real Telegram/WhatsApp gap where adapter-side concierge routing dropped `chat_queued` events, so queued messages could be acknowledged and then never deliver the eventual response. `app.py` now relays queued response buses back through the adapter bridge with an immediate queue acknowledgment; `ConcurrentDispatcher` now drains chained overflow queues correctly after a slot/resource frees up; and pinned response buses stay stable for long queued waits instead of being TTL-reaped into a replacement queue. Also upgraded concierge reassurance text to use request summaries / active `ProgressSession` phase detail instead of always sending the same canned `"Working on your request..."` line. Added focused regressions covering adapter queued-bus relay, chained overflow delivery, long bus lifetime, and phase-aware reassurance (`115 passed` across progress/dispatcher/reassurance suites).
- [docs] **Documented Telegram/WhatsApp long-response and missing-reply bugs.** User-reported: very long response times with only generic "Working on your request" every 15s (no progressive updates), and some messages never answered. Root causes: 31-14 phase-event wiring not yet in concierge; same-project message serialization; possible duplicate reassurance messages on Telegram. Added to bugs.md.
- [docs] **Reconciled Phase 21 tracking after the scheduled-dispatch coverage hardening pass.** The last coverage patch closed the explicit cross-surface `project_id + task_id` scheduled regression, but a follow-up review confirmed that the next cleanup slice is still the open Phase 21 live-wiring backlog rather than a new phase. Updated `docs/todo.md`, `docs/bugs.md`, and `docs/plans/31-daily-use-qol.md` to distinguish shipped core modules from the still-partial runtime wiring: real `/goal` execution, schedule/run-completion follow-up trigger emission, phase-event-driven progress updates, and computer-use capability/controller exposure.
- [fix] **Live concierge memory extraction now honors model-name config and no longer drops async writes.** Two production gaps were blocking the feature even after `DAN_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_LLM` was turned on: the extractor treated `DAN_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_LLM=<model-name>` as disabled unless the value was literally `1`, and the async concierge fan-out still called the deleted `_try_heuristic_extraction` helper so background fact/preference extraction failed silently while only episode memories landed. Fixed by letting `DAN_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_LLM` accept either an enable flag or a concrete model name, routing both sync and async concierge memory paths through `extract_with_llm()` with heuristic fallback, and re-running focused plus broader concierge/memory regressions (`168 passed`). Live verification on a fresh restarted server also confirmed durable memory growth (`fact: 4→5`, `preference: 11→12`) and working `/corrections` + `/adaptations` command responses.
- [fix] **Phase 21 audit hardening closed several command-surface and completion seams.** Adapter `/help` now renders commands for the actual messaging surface instead of always showing the CLI list, adapters keep server-owned `/status` and `/cancel` as raw slash commands so registry fast-dispatch still applies, dispatcher queue bypass now treats all registry chat commands as immediate commands instead of relying on a stale prefix tuple, `/cancel` now has a real registry-backed fast handler, and completion-guard follow-up text for missed action/deliverable requirements is appended instead of being silently dropped. Added focused regressions in `tests/test_concierge/test_phase31_review_hardening.py` and re-ran that targeted suite (`5 passed`).
- [fix] **Residual Phase 21 scheduler/progress cleanup closed two more cross-session leaks.** Project-only scheduled trigger contexts now resolve and persist against the intended existing project/task even when the dispatched scheduled message no longer carries the original `external_id`, using project-id-based any-surface fallback lookup in both resolution and store writes. `/progress` verbosity overrides are no longer process-global; they are now scoped to the requesting `external_id`, so one surface no longer silently changes progress rendering for every other active conversation. Added focused regressions, including runtime persistence checks for both project-only and explicit `project_id + task_id` scheduled dispatches, and re-ran the combined runtime/context/scheduler/progress/fast-command suite (`252 passed`).
- [fix] **Concierge routing now uses a safer hybrid classifier and avoids two real user-facing dead ends.** The first LLM-classifier pass exposed two issues in live chat traces: (1) auto-resolving the classifier model from provider tiers could pick a provider-specific micro model such as `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022` even when the runtime only had a generic `default` provider backed by `vectorengine.ai`, causing the classifier call to fail and silently fall back; and (2) `EXPERIENCE_QUERY` requests with no matches ended with the dead-end reply `"No similar workflows found."` instead of helping the user. Fixed by shifting `classify_intent_llm()` to a hybrid flow that trusts strong heuristic matches first (including new topical `status/progress of X` guards that keep messages like "track the progress of the Belt and Road Initiative" in normal conversation routing), using the configured chat model as classifier fallback whenever only the generic default provider is present, and making `ExperienceHandler` fall back to a helpful chat response when history search returns no matches. Added focused regressions for keyword bypass, default-provider model fallback, topical progress phrasing, and no-match experience fallback; re-ran focused runtime/handler/classifier tests (`69 passed`) plus the broad concierge suite (`976 passed`, 1 warning).
- [fix] **Phase 21 follow-up cleanup removed several more drift-prone edges.** `learning.py` no longer eagerly imports heavy engine modules just to render `/corrections` and `/adaptations`, `ExecutionContext` now exposes public `run_id` / `workflow_id` accessors plus `pii_session_key()` so `LLMExecutor` stops reaching into private fields, executor-side PII wrapping now fails closed instead of silently falling back to the raw provider when privacy protection is enabled, Telegram fleet startup lock acquisition now both caps retries and preserves fresh pending lock files during the PID-write race window, concierge fast-command dispatch now resolves handlers from the command registry so registry-only chat commands no longer fall through to the LLM path, and CLI-only REPL commands like `/show` and `/list` are no longer advertised to Telegram surfaces. Added focused regressions plus broader targeted suites (`124 passed` total across concierge, engine, and adapter files).
- [fix] **Desktop-control OCR script now quotes the screenshot path before embedding it in AppleScript.** The first post-review hardening pass quoted interactive AppleScript inputs but left the OCR helper path interpolated directly in the placeholder Vision script. Added `_build_ocr_script()` to route the screenshot path through `_apple_script_quote()` and added a focused regression for malicious quote-bearing paths. Re-ran `tests/test_tools/test_desktop_control.py` (`21 passed`).
- [feat] **Intent classifier upgraded from keyword-only to LLM-primary with keyword fallback.** The old `classify_intent()` relied entirely on substring keyword matching, which was too greedy (e.g. bare `"status"` matching in "Panama canal expansion project status" → misrouted to `StatusHandler` → "No active runs"). Added `classify_intent_llm()` as the primary classifier: uses a micro-tier LLM call (gpt-4o-mini / haiku / flash, ~200ms, ~$0.00003/call) with a compact system prompt to classify intent semantically. Fast paths (filesystem path detection, exact command phrases, polite send patterns) still bypass the LLM. On LLM failure or unparseable response, falls back to keyword classifier. Wired into Concierge runtime via `_classify_llm_complete()` helper that resolves the provider registry's micro-tier model. New `DAN_CLASSIFIER_MODEL` env var overrides the auto-resolved model. Also hardened the keyword fallback: replaced bare `"status"`/`"progress"` with specific system-status phrases and added `_has_filesystem_path()` early-exit. 28 classifier tests (966 concierge total), all passing.
- [fix] **Phase 21 post-review hardening closed several real runtime safety/correctness gaps.** Desktop-control AppleScript targets are now quoted before interpolation, browser downloads require a trigger callback instead of timing out on a no-op `expect_download()` block, scheduled runs preserve real trigger context instead of inventing synthetic task IDs, and project-only trigger contexts once again resolve to the current task. Follow-up hardening also made `/goal` fast commands retain per-surface state across `/goal-status` and `/goal-stop`, restricted `~/.dan/sensitive_words.json` to `0600`, rejected unsafe SQLite JSON filter keys, and stopped weak correction signals from producing learning actions. Added focused regressions across desktop/browser control, scheduler/context resolution, fast commands, PII persistence, and learning filters; targeted suite now passes (`356 passed, 1 skipped`).
- [fix] **Telegram fleet now deduplicates cross-bot copies of the same group message before routing.** Fresh live traces showed a single human group message reaching all four bot adapters with different per-bot `message_id`s, so the old `(chat_id, message_id)` dedup key let all four callbacks through and each one routed to the default `chief` bot. Added a bot-agnostic inbound dedup fingerprint for non-private Telegram messages and kept outbound `(chat_id, message_id)` dedup for bot echoes. Added focused regressions for cross-bot group-copy collapse and for adapter-side ingress-key generation; re-ran the Telegram adapter/fleet suite (`41 passed`).
- [fix] **Telegram adapter now avoids two recurring Bot API 400s.** `set_my_commands()` now publishes only Telegram-safe command names (lowercase letters, digits, underscores; hyphenated registry commands are skipped for Telegram menus instead of causing startup `400 Bad Request` errors), and reaction setting now disables itself per chat after the first Telegram `BadRequest` so unsupported chats do not spam repeated `setMessageReaction` failures. Added focused regressions for Telegram command filtering and reaction backoff, and re-ran the Telegram adapter/fleet suite (`30 passed`).

- [fix] **Telegram fleet startup is now single-instance guarded.** Added a `~/.dan/telegram/fleet.lock` startup lock in `run_fleet()` so a second `dan-bot start-all` cannot silently poll the same bot tokens. - [fix] **Telegram fleet hardening: stop bot self-echo loops and recover from stale reply targets.** Fixed two remaining group-chat bugs after the initial Telegram cleanup. First, `BotFleet` now ignores bot-authored messages even when Telegram does not set the usual bot flag, by checking known fleet bot usernames in both `from_user` and `sender_chat` metadata; this prevents chief/scholar/etc. from re-consuming their own outgoing group messages and recursively triggering new `/api/chat/message` requests. Second, Telegram send paths now retry once without `reply_to_message_id` when Telegram rejects `"Message to be replied not found"`, so streamed/final replies still land instead of aborting the dispatch. Added focused regressions for fleet callback filtering, sender-chat context extraction, and reply fallback handling.

- [fix] **Telegram fleet: fix repetitive bot responses and allowed_users validation.** Three fixes: (1) `send_or_edit` now handles Telegram "message is not modified" errors gracefully instead of falling back to a new message, preventing duplicate sends during streaming edits. (2) `_stream_with_edits` finalization prefers `complete_content` as the authoritative final response instead of appending it to streamed tokens, which caused duplicate content when the multi-turn tool loop generated intermediate filler. When using `complete_content`, the existing message is edited in-place with the clean final text. (3) `allowed_users` in `TelegramBotConfig` now accepts both integer user IDs and string usernames (case-insensitive, `@`-prefix tolerant), fixing the `ValidationError` when putting Telegram usernames in the config.

## 2026-03-09 (late)
- [feat] **Prompt audit — lift CONVERSATION_PROMPT + wire MCP tool hint into system prompts.** Three patches: (1) `CONVERSATION_PROMPT` was 15 thin lines with only 4 tool references; replaced with a full-coverage prompt that inherits the complete tool registry, all 4 non-negotiable rules, and the research/report behaviour section, matching `UNIFIED_SYSTEM_PROMPT` quality. (2) `CAPABILITY_TOOLS_REFERENCE` gained a `{mcp_block}` interpolation slot so dynamically registered MCP server tools appear as a **Domain tools (MCP):** section whenever servers are connected. (3) `ChatManager._compose_mcp_tools_block()` helper reads connected MCP tools via `get_mcp_tool_hint(bridge)` from `mcp_bridge`; wired into both the LLM-first path (appended after user-context block) and the legacy mode-specific path (inside `CAPABILITY_TOOLS_REFERENCE`). The MCP block is silently omitted when no servers are connected, keeping the prompt clean.
- [perf] **Fast-command path: slash commands respond instantly without LLM/memory prep.** Commands (`/save`, `/build-status`, `/build-stop`, `/memory-stats`, `/memory-search`, `/mcp *`, preference confirmations) now skip the expensive parallel prep phase (memory retrieval, context resolution, speculative reuse search) in `Concierge.process()`. New `_is_fast_command()` + `_try_fast_command()` dispatch commands before any async work. Dispatcher bypass list extended to include all command prefixes so they also skip queueing. 31 tests in `tests/test_concierge/test_fast_commands.py`.
- [fix] **Adapter forwards unknown slash commands to server instead of rejecting.** `/mcp list` (and other concierge-handled commands like `/save`, `/build-*`, `/memory-*`) were blocked by the WhatsApp adapter with "Unknown command" because `_translate_slash_command` didn't know them. Now unrecognized `/` commands pass through to the server where the concierge dispatches them. Also added `/mcp` to `/help` output.
- [feat] **29-2 §7: Long-running turn reassurance.** If a user query hasn't produced a response within 5 seconds, the concierge now yields a calming progress note ("Working on your request — this might take a moment…") before the real answer arrives. Subsequent stalls emit periodic updates every 15 s with rotating messages. Implemented via `process()` → `_process_inner()` wrapper with `asyncio.Queue` + timeout. Configurable via `DAN_CONCIERGE_REASSURANCE_DELAY` (default 5) and `DAN_CONCIERGE_REASSURANCE_INTERVAL` (default 15). Disabled when delay=0. 7 tests in `tests/test_server/test_concierge_reassurance.py`.
- [feat] **29-9: MCP Tool Bridge — consume external MCP servers as chat tools.** New `src/dan/mcp_bridge.py` module: `MCPBridge` class manages stdio `ClientSession` connections to external MCP servers, `MCPConfig`/`MCPServerConfig` Pydantic models persist config at `~/.dan/mcp.json` (Cursor/Claude Desktop compatible `mcpServers` key format), `register_mcp_tools()` / `unregister_mcp_tools()` bridge tools into both `ChatCapabilityRegistry` and `ToolRegistry`, `KNOWN_MCP_SERVERS` maps short names (e.g., `stata` → `mcp-stata`), `install_mcp_package()` runs pip as subprocess. Chat commands `/mcp install|list|remove|tools` wired into `Concierge.process()`. Added `unregister()` and `unregister_by_category()` to `ChatCapabilityRegistry`. Added `mcp_bridge` field to `CapabilityContext`. Startup auto-connect via `chat_factory.py` and `build_concierge()`. 30 tests in `tests/test_mcp_bridge.py`.

## 2026-03-09
- [fix] **RunHandler no longer starts useless runs on empty graphs.** `handle_start_run` in `capability_handlers.py` now returns early with a clear message when the workflow has no nodes. `RunHandler` in `handlers.py` now accepts a `chat_manager` and falls back to `DirectTaskHandler` (LLM+tools) when `start_run` fails, so messages like "run it" on an empty adapter workflow get a real AI response instead of an instant no-op run. Also reset the broken `_adapter_swhatsappnet` graph (had orphan nodes, missing output ports on for_each sub-graph) to empty so the adapter uses the direct chat path.

- [fix] **WhatsApp paper summary no longer returns raw PDF text.** Three-part fix: (1) `FileHandler._review_document` in `handlers.py` now strips the adapter-generated "Please review this PDF: /path" and "[User sent file: ...]" prefix lines from `msg.text` via new `_extract_user_intent()` helper, and rebuilds the review_message with truthful truncation wording ("full extracted text" vs. "extracted excerpt" capped at 12,000 chars). (2) `ChatManager.send_message()` / `_build_messages()` now accept `extra_system_instructions`, and the WhatsApp PDF-review path uses that to add a system-priority override that inline document text already counts as read source material, resolving the old contradiction with `UNIFIED_SYSTEM_PROMPT` rule #2 ("NEVER summarize a file you haven't read — call pdf_read first"). (3) `SURFACE_HINTS` for `whatsapp` and `whatsapp-web` now include "Never reproduce raw extracted text from pdf_read or file_read — always produce a structured summary or answer." Added focused regressions for `_extract_user_intent()`, truncated-excerpt prompt wording, system-level override injection, and WhatsApp surface-hint coverage.


- [fix] **Chat auto-mode detection crashed on `list_runs()` dict access.** `_produce()` in `app.py` used attribute access (`r.graph_id`, `r.status.value`) on run snapshots returned by `list_runs()`, which are dicts. Every `mode="auto"` request with a non-null `_run_manager` crashed with `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'graph_id'`. Fixed to use `.get()` dict access. Also added `logger.exception()` to the `_produce()` catch-all so future errors show tracebacks in server logs.

- [fix] **MutationPlan validation crash when LLM nests add_edge fields inside `config`.** The LLM sometimes generates `add_edge` ops like `{"op": "add_edge", "config": {"source_id": ..., "target_id": ...}}` instead of flat top-level fields. `_normalize_generated_mutation_ops` previously skipped `add_edge` ops entirely. Now lifts `source_id`, `source_port`, `target_id`, `target_port` from `config` to top level and removes the spurious `config` key, preventing `pydantic.ValidationError` crashes.

- [fix] **WhatsApp chat responses no longer contain raw HTML.** Three-layer fix: (1) `web_fetch` tool now converts HTML pages to plain text before returning to the LLM, eliminating the root source of HTML in tool results. (2) `strip_html_for_messaging()` in `concierge/actions.py` defensively strips any residual HTML tags from responses before they reach messaging surfaces — converts headings to bold, list items to bullets, links to text+URL. (3) `SURFACE_HINTS` for WhatsApp now explicitly forbid HTML tags and instruct the LLM to summarize web content in plain text.

- [fix] **Final 29-7 parity patch: media tools are now exposed to chat capabilities.** Added `image_describe` and `audio_transcribe` capability handlers/registrations so the chat capability layer more closely matches the built-in media tool set. `audio_transcribe` now returns `duration_seconds` to match the documented contract. Added focused capability tests for both handlers and registry exposure, and clarified the 29-7 note that optional-dependency media tools fail clearly when API keys or SDKs are missing.

- [test] **29-7 task 8-5: Hermetic graceful-failure coverage for media tools.** Added focused tests in `tests/test_tools/test_builtin_tools.py` for `image_describe` and `audio_transcribe` covering missing API keys and simulated missing `openai` import, using tiny local dummy files plus `monkeypatch`/import patching only. Also narrowed the `openpyxl` skip to the spreadsheet test class so optional spreadsheet deps no longer suppress unrelated built-in tool coverage.

- [feat] **29-6 tasks 7-2 to 7-7: Prompt optimization pipeline.** New `PromptAnalyzer` analyzes prompt/outcome pairs after N runs (default 20), computing success rate, token/latency averages, and failure pattern extraction (keywords in >=20% of failure outputs). `PromptVariantGenerator` produces heuristic variants via three strategies: add step-by-step (success rate < 80%), reinforce output format (format-related failures), simplify (successful runs use fewer tokens). `PromptABTest` manages A/B testing as `WORKING_STATE` items with deterministic IDs; tracks both variant and original baseline runs; `check_promotion()` requires min_runs for all arms; `promote()` stores old prompt in EPISODE provenance for rollback. `_is_safe_variant()` rejects variants removing constraint markers (MUST, REQUIRED, schema, DO NOT, NEVER) or code-fence blocks. All gated by `DAN_PROMPT_OPTIMIZATION=1`. 53 tests in `tests/test_engine/test_prompt_optimization.py`.

- [feat] **29-6 task 1-5: LLM-based memory extraction.** New `extract_with_llm()` async method on `MemoryExtractor` uses OpenAI-compatible API for nuanced fact/preference/episode detection. Gated by `DAN_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_LLM=1` (default `0`). Falls back to heuristic extraction when: env var is off, no API key available, `openai` package not installed, or any LLM error. `_parse_llm_response()` handles JSON arrays and markdown-fenced code blocks. 10 new tests covering env-var gating, no-key fallback, JSON parsing (valid, empty, invalid, markdown-fenced, invalid types, empty content, multiple items).

- [feat] **29-6 task 2-6: Reflection-based principle extraction for new failure patterns.** New `_maybe_extract_new_principle()` on `RunLearner` checks existing principles for coverage of the error category; if uncovered, creates a low-confidence (0.3) principle with error context and workflow node types. Wired into both sync `_on_failure()` and async `extract_run_learnings_async()` failure paths. 7 new tests covering: new category extraction, existing-tag coverage skip, metadata-based coverage, workflow node types in content, no-workflow extraction, end-to-end wiring through `extract_run_learnings`, and duplicate-prevention with boost.

- [feat] **29-6 tasks 5-1..5-5, 6-1..6-5: Generation feedback loop and preference evolution.** New `src/dan/engine/generation_stats.py` with `GenerationStats` Pydantic model tracking per-pattern/per-method success rates and common failure modes, persisted as a single `WORKING_STATE` item in memory kernel. `record_generation_outcome()` convenience fires from `ChatManager._generate_workflow_from_intent()` after intent-compiler, codegen, and diagnosis loop outcomes. `format_for_prompt()` injects "common mistakes to avoid" into codegen prompts. `adjust_reuse_score()` boosts reuse scores for patterns that fail during generation (making reuse more attractive) and slightly reduces scores for easily-generated patterns; wired into `DiscoveryService.discover_workflows()`. Preference evolution: `MemoryKernel.store_preference()` now runs `_resolve_preference_conflicts()` — explicit user statements archive conflicting inferred prefs, inferred prefs demote (halve importance of) older inferred ones. `maybe_surface_preferences(session_count)` returns top-5 unconfirmed preferences every N interactions (`DAN_PREFERENCE_SURFACE_INTERVAL`, default 10). `confirm_preference()` boosts to importance=1.0 + DURABLE lifecycle; `reject_preference()` archives with `rejected_by_user` metadata. Concierge runtime gains `_maybe_surface_preferences()` and `handle_preference_confirmation()` for the full confirm/reject flow. 27 tests in `tests/test_engine/test_generation_stats.py` covering stats recording, pattern success rates, common failures, prompt formatting, reuse score adjustment (high/low success), persistence round-trip, preference conflict resolution (confirmed→archive, inferred→demote), surfacing interval/env-var/skipping, and confirm-boost/reject-archive semantics.

- [feat] **29-6 tasks 7-1, 7-8, 8-1..8-8, 10-1..10-6: Outcome trackers for prompt, model, and topology learning.** New `src/dan/engine/outcome_trackers.py` with five classes: `PromptTracker` records (node_id, prompt_hash, input/output summary, outcome, tokens, latency) as EPISODE items for future prompt optimization (gated by `DAN_PROMPT_OPTIMIZATION=1`). `ModelOutcomeTracker` records per-execution model telemetry; `ModelRecommender` computes empirical scores (`quality*0.6 + (1-cost)*0.2 + (1-latency)*0.2`) and suggests best model per node after 15+ executions, persisting recommendations as PREFERENCE items (scope=WORKFLOW, lifecycle=DURABLE) for cross-session persistence (gated by `DAN_MODEL_LEARNING=1`). `TopologyOutcomeTracker` records (topology_signature, outcome, failure_node, failure_type) reusing `PatternExtractor._compute_signature()`; `TopologyAdvisor` identifies failure hotspots and suggests structural improvements like adding validators after high-failure-rate LLM nodes (gated by `DAN_TOPOLOGY_LEARNING=1`). All trackers wired into `RunManager._enrich_and_persist()` as fire-and-forget after every run. Override hierarchy: explicit per-node model > empirical recommendation > TierPolicy > default. 35 tests in `tests/test_engine/test_outcome_trackers.py` covering env-var gating, record/retrieve, hash determinism, quality scoring, recommendation with sufficient/insufficient data, preference persistence/update, topology signature determinism, validator suggestion logic, and suggestion outcome tracking.

- [feat] **29-5 tasks 5, 9, 10: Parallel memory extraction, unified queue, and immediate-start guarantee.** `_store_memory_candidates()` now schedules a fire-and-forget background `asyncio.Task` that fans out episode, preference, and heuristic extraction concurrently via `fan_out_dict` + `asyncio.to_thread`. Falls back to sync when no event loop. `ProjectMessageQueue` (`queue.py`) deprecated as a no-op pass-through — `ConcurrentDispatcher` is now the single authority for all queueing/serialization. Removed `skip_queue` metadata flag from runtime and dispatcher. `_drain_queued_messages` is now a no-op (dispatcher owns draining). Dispatcher gains `_is_bypass_command()` so `/status`, `/build-status`, `/cancel`, `/build-stop` always process immediately regardless of project activity. `ChatQueuedEvent` extended with `queue_position` field. 23 tests in `tests/test_concierge/test_unified_queue.py` covering concurrent extraction steps, partial failure tolerance, sync fallback, deprecated queue pass-through, immediate-start for new projects, same-project serialization, cross-project concurrency, status/cancel bypass, and queue position info.

Both project-level and global overflow queues replaced with `PriorityQueue` so higher-priority messages are dequeued first. Backward compatible: without a `ResourceTracker`, legacy hard cap behavior is unchanged. 37 tests in `tests/test_concierge/test_resources.py`; all 260 concierge tests pass.

This gives adapter users the same reuse-first behavior, intent classification, and goal orchestration as CLI/server users. Message callback is now always registered (not gated on graph presence), with fallback to legacy Engine path when no dispatcher is available. Added `/workflows` adapter command that lists saved workflows formatted for the messaging surface. New `_adapter_surface_types` tracking maps adapter IDs to surface names. 16 tests in `tests/test_adapters/test_adapter_parity.py` covering SurfaceMessage construction, dispatcher routing, `/workflows` command, metadata preservation, and app-level integration.

- [feat] **29-6 tasks 4-1 to 4-6: Structural pattern extraction.** New `src/dan/engine/pattern_extractor.py` with `PatternExtractor` class. Computes deterministic topology signatures from workflow graphs (node type counts + sorted edge type pairs), finds signatures recurring in 2+ workflows, and stores them as `WORKFLOW_PATTERN` memory items with `lifecycle=ACTIVE`. Idempotent — re-running with the same data updates occurrence counts instead of duplicating. Patterns link back to source workflows via `related_ids` (4-6). `should_run()` gate checks `WORKFLOW_ASSET` count against a configurable threshold (default 10). Wired into `MemoryKernel.run_consolidation(graph_store=...)` so extraction runs during the periodic consolidation schedule. Updated return dict to include `patterns_extracted` count. 24 tests in `tests/test_engine/test_pattern_extractor.py` covering signature determinism, threshold gating, common-pattern finding, deduplication, related_ids merging, end-to-end extraction, and consolidation integration.

The async DIAGNOSING path keeps per-source fallbacks intact, builds a combined `diagnosis_context`, and hardens `fan_out()` so tasks that fail before returning a coroutine degrade cleanly. Added focused tests for combined diagnosis aggregation and partial-source failure fallback (`12 passed` across the diagnosis and fan-out suites).

Concierge post-build follow-ups now fan out memory persistence, workflow linking, and adapted-workflow asset writes; failures in one branch are logged without failing the whole completed turn. Also exposed `spreadsheet_read` and `text_translate` as chat capability tools. Added/updated tests for redaction and metadata persistence; broad regression suite remains green (`437 passed`).

When available, classifies errors via `ErrorClassifier`, maps artifacts, and selects correction strategies (auto_fix/re_prompt/suggest_to_user). Fully optional — lazy import with try/except fallback to memory-only diagnosis.

Registered in `register_workflow_catalog_capabilities()` for all chat modes. 9 tests in `tests/test_server/test_workflow_catalog.py`.

Added workflow catalog tools section to `llm-api-guide.md`.

- [feat] **29-6 tasks 2-1 to 2-5, 2-7, 3-1 to 3-5: Post-run learning and cross-section reinforcement.** New `src/dan/engine/run_learner.py` with `RunLearner` class. On success: creates/updates `WORKFLOW_ASSET` with success_rate, boosts matching `WORKFLOW_PATTERN` by topology detection. On failure: creates `FAILURE_PATTERN` with error category (`timeout`/`validation`/`api_error`/etc), node type, workflow_id; boosts matching `PRINCIPLE` confidence. On repair success: links repair strategy to failure pattern. Cross-section methods: `boost_reused_asset()` (boosts asset + linked patterns), `boost_preventing_principle()`, `demote_overridden_preference()`, `update_contradicted_fact()` (preserves old content in provenance). Decay verified via existing `apply_decay()`. Wired into `RunManager._enrich_and_persist()` as fire-and-forget after every run. Added `memory_kernel` param to `RunManager.__init__()`. 26 tests in `tests/test_engine/test_run_learner.py`.

- [feat] **29-6 tasks 1-1 to 1-4, 1-6, 1-7: Heuristic MemoryExtractor.** New `src/dan/engine/memory_extractor.py` with `MemoryExtractor` class that extracts FACT, PREFERENCE, and EPISODE candidates from user/assistant interactions using regex heuristics. FACT patterns: data format, file location, delimiter, schema, project context, timeline, standalone file paths. PREFERENCE patterns: explicit "I prefer X", tool preferences ("use X for Y"), behavioral ("don't ask me to confirm"), output format. EPISODE: summarized user request + tools used + outcome (capped at 300 chars). Wired into `Concierge._store_memory_candidates()` via new `_try_heuristic_extraction()` method — fires after every turn, gated by `DAN_MEMORY_EXTRACTION=1` env var (default on). Does not duplicate PreferenceExtractor (model/domain/format) or existing episode extraction. Fire-and-forget: exceptions are caught and logged. 27 tests in `tests/test_engine/test_memory_extractor.py`.

- [feat] **29-5 tasks 1, 2: Fan-out utility and parallel turn preparation.** New `src/dan/server/concierge/fan_out.py` with `fan_out()` and `fan_out_dict()` — lightweight `asyncio.gather` wrappers with per-task timeout, partial failure handling, and named-task support. Refactored `Concierge.process()` to run memory retrieval and context resolution concurrently via `asyncio.to_thread` (both are sync). Parallel path gated by `DAN_CONCIERGE_PARALLEL_PREP` env var (default `1`). Precomputed context used when no pending follow-up; discarded otherwise. Falls back to sequential on exception. Exported from concierge `__init__.py`. 10 tests in `tests/test_concierge/test_fan_out.py` (fan_out unit, dict, timeout, partial failure, order preservation, parallel/sequential prep parity). All 26 existing runtime tests unaffected.

- [feat] **29-2 tasks 3-2 to 3-6, 7-5: Goal orchestration loop wiring.** Completed the planning→execution→diagnosis→repair→check-in loop inside `Concierge._execute_goal()`. Added `_decide_plan_action()` (queries memory kernel with WORKFLOW_BUILD policy, sets `plan_action` to reuse/adapt/generate), `_diagnose_goal_failure()` (queries WORKFLOW_REPAIR policy or delegates to `BuildSessionManager.diagnose_for_failure()`), `_compose_check_in()` (filters step details by autonomy level — INTERACTIVE shows all, SUPERVISED shows failure/completion, AUTONOMOUS is minimal). Tracks `last_run_status` in goal context. Enforces repair cap via `max_iterations`. 12 integration tests in `tests/test_concierge/test_goal_orchestration.py` covering autonomous completion, planning decisions, execution tracking, diagnosis, repair cap, autonomy-based check-in, backward compat without memory kernel.

- [feat] **29-4 tasks 6-2 to 6-4: Experience feedback loop completion.** Failed reuse now stores a `FAILURE_PATTERN` in memory linking `workflow_id`, `reuse_attempt=True`, and `error_category` when a reused workflow's smoke test fails (`_handle_reuse_workflow` in `runtime.py`). Successful adaptation stores a new `WORKFLOW_ASSET` with `related_ids` pointing to the parent workflow (`_advance_build_session`). Reuse/adapt/generate decisions and applied choices are logged via `logger.info` at both decision and application points.

All 28 pass; 92 related existing tests unaffected.

Extracts model/domain/format preferences via heuristic `PreferenceExtractor` and stores as PREFERENCE items in memory kernel. Gated by `DAN_PREFERENCE_EXTRACTION` env var (default `1`).
- [test] **19 tests for consolidation + preference wiring.** New `tests/test_engine/test_consolidation.py` covers `run_consolidation()` (full lifecycle, empty kernel, stale archival, decay), `_consolidation_loop` (runs/cancels, handles errors), env var parsing, and `_try_extract_preferences` (models, domains, format, no-op, disabled, no kernel, error handling, integration with `_store_memory_candidates`).

Changed to single braces in `src/dan/tools/python_eval.py`. Removed xfail markers from 2 tests; both now pass.

- [docs] **Reconciled Phase 29 plans with the current codebase and added a practical research/audit sub-plan.** Updated the Phase 19 parent plan to `in-progress`, added [29-8](plans/29-8-practical-research-quality-and-audit.md) for daily-use acceptance on equity research, deep research, PDF literature summary, and literature search with gated-paper handoff, and patched stale plan/todo text so `29-1` and `29-7` reflect shipped work while `29-2` through `29-4` now call out the real remaining gaps. - [fix] **Follow-up test stabilization for Phase 28/29 chat changes.** Fixed the `ChatManager._build_messages()` memory-kernel injection typo in both the LLM-first and legacy prompt paths (`user_message` instead of undefined `message`), which cleared the `test_build_from_intent` / `test_chat_codegen_integration` failures. Refreshed stale tests to match the current architecture: CLI integration tests now force `--local` so they do not depend on a live dev server, `MetaGoalHandler` tests mock `create_session_for_goal()`, publish/share capability tests assert mode-agnostic tool availability, and build-from-intent prompt tests now validate the unified LLM-first prompt instead of removed per-mode prompt text.

- [fix] **Phase 29 review patch: wire the real orchestrator path, persist build sessions, and expose `pdf_read` vision mode in chat.** Concierge now routes `workflow_build`/`meta_goal` turns into the Phase 29 goal-orchestrator path only when both `memory_kernel` and `meta_controller` are available; server startup now wires both so the primary server path uses the new flow. Build sessions persist across follow-up turns instead of being recreated, user feedback is folded back into build memory context, `"don't test"` can skip smoke runs while explicit `"run it"` forces them, and completed workflow memories now store goal descriptions plus reuse counters. `increment_workflow_asset_usage()` now tracks real reuse attempts instead of retrieval exposure. `pdf_read` capability handlers now forward `mode/start_page/end_page/vision_*` args to the tool, vision mode returns truncation metadata/warnings when capped to 25 pages, and `pymupdf` is included in `all-tools` / `all` extras. Added 7 regression tests covering the review fixes.

Memory kernel: `increment_workflow_asset_usage(workflow_id, success)` updates access_count and success_count on WORKFLOW_ASSET; called from `_handle_reuse_workflow` after smoke test. Reuse path uses `context.project.surface_id` fallback for link_workflow.

Concierge: `/build-status` and `/build-stop` commands; user feedback on "continue" stored in build session; after MetaController produces workflow, `_advance_build_session()` runs validation and smoke test, stores post-build memory on COMPLETED/FAILED. 48 concierge tests.

- [feat] **29-3 Build session state machine and smoke testing.** `BuildSessionManager` now provides `validate_draft(graph)` (calls `validate_graph`), `generate_smoke_inputs(graph)` (from InputNode variables), and `run_smoke_test(session, graph, graph_id, run_manager)` (async, 60s timeout, skippable via `DAN_BUILD_SKIP_SMOKE=1`). Concierge creates a `BuildSession` for workflow-build goals (keywords: build/create/make/automate) and stores `build_session_id` in `goal.context`. Added `_is_workflow_build_goal()` helper. 40 concierge tests.

- [feat] **pdf_read: vision mode for figures and tables.** `pdf_read` now accepts `mode`: `"text"` (default, pypdf extraction) or `"vision"`. With `mode="vision"`, pages are rendered to images via PyMuPDF and each page is described by a vision LLM (e.g. gpt-4o), preserving figures, tables, and layout. Optional params: `vision_model`, `vision_prompt`. Capped at 25 pages per call. Added `pymupdf>=1.24` to optional `[pdf]` dependency group.

Added `create_session_for_goal(goal)` to build and persist a MetaSession from a ConciergeGoal. MetaGoalHandler now creates a ConciergeGoal, calls `create_session_for_goal(goal)`, then runs the session via `run_session` (legacy path when no memory_kernel).

Concierge normalizes `DAN_CONCIERGE_AUTONOMY` / `autonomy_level` on init. `_effective_autonomy(surface)` returns surface-specific default (WhatsApp/Telegram → autonomous, CLI/editor/server → supervised) or config. Per-goal override: `_autonomy_override_from_message()` detects "just do it"/"go ahead" → autonomous, "show me every step"/"walk me through" → interactive; stored in `goal.context["autonomy_override"]` and `goal.context["effective_autonomy"]` for new goals. Exported `AutonomyLevel` from concierge package. Five autonomy tests added.

After each response, `_extract_memory_candidates()` builds episode (+ optional failure_pattern from goal error_history); `_store_memory_candidates()` persists them to the kernel. Load/save on every `process()`. Goal lifecycle: `_detect_goal()`, `_continue_or_new()`; META_GOAL path when `memory_kernel` is present creates or continues a goal and runs `_execute_goal()` (delegates to MetaController.run_session, syncs result to ConciergeGoal; stores failures as FAILURE_PATTERN). `build_concierge()` and chat_factory now pass `memory_kernel` and optional `autonomy_level`; `DAN_CONCIERGE_AUTONOMY` env supported.

Tightened `25-7-action-autonomy-policy.md` so queue/progress language is project-aware, bounded parallel project spawning is part of policy, progress APIs use `get_project_progress()`, workflow-promotion examples use the new `[DAN - <Project>]` label format, and `AdapterConfig.auto_approve` stays as a deprecated compatibility alias instead of being removed. Patched `25-chat-control-plane.md` to reflect that 25-6/25-7 add a concierge layer above the capability/tool layer, rather than leaving the parent plan in an LLM-first routing state.

- [docs] **Phase 15 concierge subplans expanded and patched (25-6, 25-7).** Rewrote the two remaining Phase 15 sub-plans, then patched with feedback from prior brainstorming chat (transcript 0ea4e450). Key changes from patch: (1) Upgraded from single `TaskSession` to 2-layer **Project + Task** scope model — `Project` is the durable first-class scope (memory, summaries, label), `Task` is a lightweight workstream inside it (label, status, recent turns). Reply label format: `[DAN - <Project>]` by default, `[DAN - <Project> / <Task>]` when task-specific. (2) Summary-first memory loading: LLM receives project summary + recent task turns, not full chat history. Auto-summarization after every N turns or on task completion. (3) Referenced already-shipped adapter quick fixes (intent pre-routing, filename matching, ask-mode fix, docx MIME) as prototypes for shared concierge. (4) Renamed `TaskSessionStore` → `ProjectStore`, `TaskContextResolver` → `ProjectContextResolver`, `TaskMessageQueue` → `ProjectMessageQueue` throughout. Updated parent plan, todo.md, and changelog.

- [fix] **WhatsApp Web now sends `.docx` with the correct Office MIME type instead of leaving WhatsApp to infer from ZIP-like bytes.** The adapter was already sending the original `.docx` bytes, not re-zipping the file, but `WhatsAppWebAdapter.send_file()` called `neonize.send_document()` without the optional `mimetype` argument. Since `.docx` is a ZIP-based OOXML container internally, that could cause the receiving client to treat it as a generic zip/document. Added `_guess_mimetype()` and now pass the explicit MIME (for the real file: `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`) when sending documents. Added a regression test asserting `.docx` sends include the correct mimetype. Verified with `pytest tests/test_adapters/test_whatsapp_web.py -v` (17 passed) and a direct MIME check on `/Users/lizhi/Dropbox/late_payment_seasonality_20251106.docx`.

- [fix] **Adapter filename search now matches natural-language queries against underscored files.** Reproduced the real failure where `_handle_find_command("late payment seasonality")` reported no matches even though `/Users/lizhi/Dropbox/late_payment_seasonality_20251106.docx` existed. Root cause: the adapter was using a literal recursive glob pattern like `**/*late payment seasonality*`, which cannot match underscores, hyphens, or date suffixes in filenames. Added `_search_local_files()` with normalized token matching and scoring (`late payment seasonality` → `late_payment_seasonality_20251106.docx`), and reused it for both `/find` and `/send` fallback resolution. Added `tests/test_adapters/test_adapter_file_search.py` for underscore/space matching and ranking. Verified with a live local query against `~/Dropbox` and `pytest tests/test_adapters/test_adapter_chat_mode.py tests/test_adapters/test_adapter_intent.py tests/test_adapters/test_adapter_file_search.py -v` (30 passed).

- [fix] **Adapter polite file-send requests no longer fall through to fake LLM tool calls.** Reproduced the real WhatsApp phrasing `"Good. Can you send me the late payment seasonality doc file under ~/Dropbox folder?"` and found two root causes: `_classify_adapter_intent()` only matched direct imperative prefixes (`send me ...`), so polite requests fell through to `conversation`, and `ChatManager._build_messages()` still appended `CAPABILITY_TOOLS_REFERENCE` in `ask` mode even though no tools were actually executable there. Added `_extract_search_query_from_send_request()` to normalize polite send requests into local `file_search` queries (e.g. `late payment seasonality`), and restricted capability-tool prompt injection to non-`ask`/`plan` modes. Added regression tests for both failures. Verified with `pytest tests/test_adapters/test_adapter_chat_mode.py tests/test_adapters/test_adapter_intent.py -v` (28 passed) and `pytest tests/test_server/test_chat_manager.py -v` (39 passed).

- [fix] **Adapter intent pre-routing — stop sending everything through the 24-tool LLM pipeline.** The adapter's chat mode was routing every message through the server's full ChatManager (24 capability tools + mutation tool), causing the LLM to call `search_workflow_history` and `discover_capabilities` instead of doing what the user asked (e.g. finding a file). Added a lightweight heuristic intent classifier (`_classify_adapter_intent`) that routes locally before hitting the server: file requests go through `_handle_find_command`/`_handle_send_command` directly, continuations ("yes", "do it", "just do it") replay the pending action, number selections pick from listed results, and only explicit workflow-build requests go to the full tool pipeline. General conversation uses `mode=ask` (text-only, no tools) instead of `mode=auto`. Simplified `_ADAPTER_CONTEXT` prompt (4 lines instead of 25). Auto-sends single-match file results. 25 new tests in `test_adapter_intent.py`, 154 total adapter tests pass.

- [feat] **Orbis matching resume-state implementation completed.** Finished the external Orbis batch runner hardening with structured `completed` + `in_progress` progress state, stage detection (`upload-start` / `mapping` / `matching-details` / `results-details`), resume-target selection that prioritizes persisted matching work, and `_run_batch()` current-page shortcut/reopen flow so interrupted batches continue without re-upload. Added safety checks to require unambiguous target-CSV identity before shortcut/reopen (including `_1` vs `_10` collision protection), expanded tests for resume and safety edge cases, and re-verified with `python -m unittest test_orbis_batch_match.py -v` (`Ran 35 tests`, `OK`).

- [docs] **Phase 15 concierge rearchitecture plans (25-6, 25-7).** Added two new sub-plans to Phase 15 addressing the core chat UX problem: the LLM currently receives 24+ tools and decides ad-hoc which to call, producing inconsistent behavior (mutations for file requests, unnecessary questions, suggested commands instead of execution). (25-6) Deterministic intent dispatcher: heuristic classifier → registered handler per intent category → LLM only for direct conversation. 5 sub-tasks: intent taxonomy, handler registry, adapter/CLI wiring, dedicated file handler, adapter prompt simplification. (25-7) Action autonomy policy: each handler declares `auto`/`confirm`/`clarify`; default is `auto` (just do it). Confirmation only for destructive/ambiguous/expensive actions. Max one round of clarification per action.

- [fix] **WhatsApp Web incoming message handling (`MessageSource.IsFromMe` + self-message commands).** Fixed `WhatsAppWebAdapter._handle_incoming()` to read sender/origin metadata from `event.Info.MessageSource` (with a fallback to legacy `Info.IsFromMe`) instead of incorrectly assuming `IsFromMe` existed directly on `Info`. This was causing the first real incoming message after QR pairing to crash with `AttributeError: IsFromMe`, even though pairing/auth succeeded. Also refined the self-message filter for personal WhatsApp use: messages sent from your own phone are now allowed through as commands unless they match a very recent outbound DAN reply, which is treated as an echo and suppressed to avoid reply loops. Added `tests/test_adapters/test_whatsapp_web.py` covering nested `MessageSource.IsFromMe`, self-message command handling, outbound echo suppression, pending HumanNode response resolution, config defaults, session mapping, and message splitting. 9 focused tests pass.

- [fix] **Adapter chat-mode stream handling now respects `chat_complete.content`.** `dan-adapter` chat mode previously only accumulated `chat_token` events and mutation summaries, then ignored the final `chat_complete.content`. This meant requests could reach `/api/chat/message` and the LLM path successfully, but produce no visible reply on messaging surfaces when the server returned content only at completion. Extracted `_consume_chat_stream_events()` in `src/dan/cli/adapter.py` to merge streamed tokens, mutation events, and final completion content correctly. Added `tests/test_adapters/test_adapter_chat_mode.py` covering the no-token `chat_complete.content` case and the streamed-token case. 2 focused tests pass.

- [feat] **Adapter chat mode — messaging adapters as general-purpose DAN chat.** When `--workflow` is omitted, `dan-adapter` now routes messages through the server's chat API (same as `dan-chat`) instead of running a fixed workflow. Works for all adapter types: Telegram, WhatsApp Web, WhatsApp Business, email. Each messaging conversation gets its own workflow. Supports streaming responses, mutation proposals (auto-apply when `auto_approve=True`), and conversation history. Usage: `dan-adapter telegram --bot-token TOKEN` (chat mode) vs `dan-adapter telegram --bot-token TOKEN -w workflow.md` (workflow mode). Added `--server` flag for custom server URL. Updated `docs/cli.md` with chat mode documentation and Telegram setup guide.

QR code pairing — scan once, stays linked. No Business API, no Meta verification, no webhook. Session persisted in `~/.dan/whatsapp-web/`. CLI: `dan-adapter whatsapp-web -w workflow.md`. Added `whatsapp-web` subcommand to `cli/adapter.py`, `WhatsAppWebAdapterConfig` with `db_path`/`allowed_jids`, optional dep `neonize>=0.3` (`pip install 'dan[whatsapp-web]'`). Updated `docs/cli.md` with setup guide and comparison table. Follows same adapter protocol as Telegram/email (session store, HumanNode renderer, gateway mixin compatible).

The LLM receives a `load_hyperedge(name)` tool to fetch full skill/rule content on demand. Added `_summarize_hyperedge()`, `get_hyperedge_content()`, JIT-aware `apply_pre_prompt()` returning `(messages, jit_tool_needed)`, `HYPEREDGE_JIT_TOOL` schema, and `load_hyperedge` handling in `LLMExecutor._execute_tool_call()`. 12 tests in `test_hyperedge_jit.py`; existing hyperedge tests updated for tuple return.

Wired into `LLMExecutor` via optional `context.tier_tracker`; records success/failure after each LLM call and logs de-escalation suggestions. Tracker initialized from `{memory_dir}/tier_stats.json` in app lifespan. 9 tests in `test_tier_tracker.py`.

## 2026-03-05

- [fix] **Additional chat-plan schema normalization for validator and edge-type drift.** Extended `_normalize_generated_mutation_ops()` to coerce `validator.config.on_failure` aliases (`retry`→`route`, `continue/ignore`→`warn`, `stop/fail`→`halt`) and to convert generated `add_edge` ops with `edge_type: "context"` into `data` edges in chat mode. This avoids Graph parse failures from context-edge fields that are not represented in chat mutation tool ops.

- [fix] **Auto-normalize common planner schema drift (`parallel_subagents`, `validator`) in chat mutation ops.** Added `_normalize_generated_mutation_ops()` in `chat_manager` and applied it to tool-calling plans (initial/retry/replan/fallback) before `MutationPlan` validation. Repairs frequent invalid outputs such as `parallel_subagents.branch_graphs` dict→list, `branch_inputs` string→dict, and validator `rule_type: required_field(s)` → `required_keys` with normalized `config.keys`. This prevents repeated dry-run parse failures and improves repair convergence.

- [fix] **Streamlined `dan-chat` mutation flow: auto-repair loop + no apply prompt on failed dry-run.** `send_message_with_tools()` now performs multi-attempt auto-repair (`DAN_MUTATION_AUTO_RETRY_MAX`, default 2) when dry-run fails, carrying forward the latest attempted plan/result so users see the newest candidate. In CLI, `dan-chat` now skips the apply prompt when `dry_run_result.success` is false and asks for a follow-up repair instead of letting users trigger predictable apply failures. Added regression tests in `tests/test_server/test_build_from_intent.py` and `tests/test_cli/test_chat.py`.

- [fix] **Build-mode strict edge coercion removed for generated plans.** `dan-chat` build mode previously forced `strict=True` on all generated `add_edge` ops (`_coerce_strict_edges`), which caused valid plans to fail when routing semantic inputs into downstream nodes (`fundamental_analysis`, `sentiment_analysis`, `recommendation`, etc.). Updated `_coerce_strict_edges` to preserve edge strictness as generated (no forced strict), allowing auto-created target input ports when appropriate. Updated regression tests in `tests/test_server/test_build_from_intent.py`.

- [fix] **Input-port wiring compatibility for `dan-chat` generated plans.** Some generated mutation plans wired `source_port: "input"` from Input nodes that declared variable outputs (`ticker`, `company_name`, etc.), causing apply failures (`Source node 'node_input' has no output port 'input'`). Fixed by: (1) mutator default ports for variable-based Input nodes now include aggregate `input` output alongside per-variable outputs; (2) add-edge compatibility path auto-creates missing `input` output on existing Input nodes; (3) Input executor now emits aggregate `outputs["input"]` payload (dict of resolved variables). Added regression tests in `tests/test_server/test_graph_mutator.py` and `tests/test_engine/test_input_executor.py`.

- [fix] **Mutation apply always failed with stale revision + node ID mismatch.** Two root causes fixed: (1) `compute_graph_revision` hashed the raw graph dict from disk, while ChatManager round-tripped through Pydantic first (adding default fields). Fixed by normalizing through `Graph.model_validate()` inside `compute_graph_revision()`. (2) LLM-generated mutation plans used `node_1`, `node_2`, etc. as IDs, but `add_node` slugified names (`Research Input` -> `research-input`). Fixed by: adding `id` field to `AddNode` model + tool schema so LLM can specify stable IDs; building sequential alias table (`node_N` -> actual slug) during plan application so old-style references resolve automatically. Also: `apply_mutation` returns `graph_revision`; WebSocket sends explicit close frame; `dan-serve` reload watcher excludes `graphs/`, `runs/`, `checkpoints/`.

Added full human input handling in REPL (prompt, approval/text modes, submit via new `ChatClient.submit_human_input()`). `_pipe_run_events` now breaks on `run_cancelled` (was 300s hang).   - Extended `CheckpointData` model in `engine/checkpoint.py` with `graph_revision` (deterministic hash of graph nodes + edges), `completed_node_ids`, and `node_outputs` fields. Updated `Engine._save_checkpoint()` to populate these fields on every checkpoint write.

  - `check_checkpoint_staleness()`: compares checkpoint's `graph_revision` to current graph, returns `StalenessResult` with `compatible`, `stale`, `missing_nodes`, and `message` fields.
  - `compute_downstream_nodes()`: BFS traversal from target node to find all downstream dependents for `downstream_of` scope.
  - `compute_subgraph_node_ids()`: looks up sub-graph by key and returns node IDs for `subgraph` scope.

  - `RunManager.get_checkpoint_info()` and `list_checkpoint_runs()`: query checkpoint metadata for API consumption.

  - `RERUN_STARTED` event type: emitted before partial rerun execution with full provenance (`source_checkpoint_id`, `rerun_scope`, `nodes_to_rerun`, `nodes_skipped`). Result metadata tagged with `__rerun_provenance__`.

- [docs] **Plan 18 philosophy rework — no brute-force, agent-directed, externalized state.** Major reframe of all five token-optimization plans after competitive landscape review (Cursor, MemGPT/Letta, Beads, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, LangChain ACE, GPTCache, LLMLingua, production patterns). Key changes:
  - **18 (high-level):** Added "Design Philosophy" section establishing three principles: (1) agent-controlled context (MemGPT pattern), (2) externalized structured state (Beads pattern), (3) mechanical format efficiency. Renamed sub-plans: 18-1 → "Smart Context Assembly", 18-3 → "Agent-Directed Context Architecture". Updated success criteria to ban brute-force truncation.
  - **18-1:** Renamed from "Prompt Compression" to "Smart Context Assembly." Reframed `max_input_tokens` as advisory `target_input_tokens` (never blocks). Replaced `ContextPruner` with `ContextSelector` (defers low-relevance inputs to tool-accessible storage, never deletes). Added 3 new tasks: (7) JIT tool/schema loading — 20-40% context savings on tool-heavy workflows; (8) Schema/format pruning — mechanically strip unused fields, optional compact serialization; (9) Agent context tools (MemGPT pattern) — `search_context`, `read_context`, `read_state`, `list_available_context`.
  - **18-2:** Added query normalization before semantic cache embedding (GPTCache pattern — 61-68% hit rates).
  - **18-3:** Renamed from "Context Window Management" to "Agent-Directed Context Architecture." - [feat] **LLM-driven OrchestratorExecutor (16-5).** Rewrote `OrchestratorExecutor` in `executors/control_flow.py` as a true event-driven LLM orchestrator. The orchestrator LLM is invoked reactively when teams complete, using two tool calls: `dispatch_to_team(team_name, inputs)` to start team sub-graphs and `halt_orchestrator(reason, final_result)` to cleanly exit. Conversation history accumulates system prompt + initial inputs + team completion events as user messages. Concurrency management prevents re-dispatching already-running teams (error feedback to LLM). Safety bounds via `max_llm_calls` and `max_iterations`. Falls back to static fan-out when `orchestrator_prompt`/`orchestrator_model` are unset (backward compat). All 11 existing orchestrator tests pass unchanged.

- [docs] **Decompiler control/context semantics documented (Plan 7-8 Task 7):** In `docs/llm-api-guide.md` section 12b (Markdown Authoring Guidance), strengthened the context-heavy workflows bullet: control and context edges are emitted as `<!-- SKIPPED -->` comments; round-trip is not lossless for those workflows. LLM callers should keep a Python/JSON canonical source for full round-trip of context-heavy or control-heavy workflows.
- [feat] **Flow parse strict mode + ambiguous bare-edge fail (Plan 7-8 Tasks 4 & 6):** Added `strict: bool = False` to `compile_workflow()` and `load()`. When `strict=True`: (1) parse_warnings become fatal errors and compilation stops with `graph=None`; (2) ambiguous bare-edge auto-wire (multiple matching ports) emits error instead of warning. Non-strict keeps backward compatibility. Improved hint: "Use explicit 'A.port_x → B.port_y' to wire all intended ports." Updated `docs/llm-api-guide.md` 12a: recommend `strict=True` for LLM-generated and new workflows. Added `TestStrictMode` tests.

NodeRef stores `gate_mode`; builder `wf.gate()` passes it. Decompiler `_is_default_data_edge` passes gate_mode for gate nodes. Updated `docs/llm-api-guide.md` 12a rule 3: `gate >> body` works; explicit `gate["continue"]` still recommended for clarity.
- [fix] **ContextEdge read validation aligned with runtime (Plan 7-8 Task 2):** `_check_context_edge_permissions` now validates READ mode against the **target** node's `read_set` (consumer), not the source's. WRITE/APPEND still validate the source's `write_set`. Added `test_read_validates_target_not_source` to lock in correct behavior. Updated `docs/llm-api-guide.md` with context-edge semantics: read = target consumes, write = source produces.

## 2026-02-27
- [docs] **LLM generation playbook added to API guide:** Expanded `docs/llm-api-guide.md` with a dedicated workflow/script generation section (explicit typing/wiring rules, gate-loop authoring guidance, markdown vs Python generation caveats, and a recommended generate→compile→validate→smoke-test loop) to reduce silent miswiring and improve reproducibility for LLM-authored workflows.
- [feat] **Custom strategy script artifacts are now persisted before execution:** `_run_strategy_script` now saves incoming code to `examples/vibe_research_md/output/scripts/{strategy}.py` before running it, and returns `script_saved_path`/`script_save_error`. Workflow nodes were updated so these fields survive error normalization (`bug_fixer`) and are passed through persistence/output (`save_tracking`), making custom-factor runs directly reproducible.
- [fix] **CRSP formation-universe price filter enforced (`|price| >= 1`)**: Added canonical CRSP price aliases (`close_price_month`/`prc`), threaded `min_price` through builtin backtest CLI/tool path, and applied the same threshold in custom-factor backtests by auto-attaching CRSP formation prices by `(date, permno)` when missing. This removes sub-$1 names at portfolio formation while keeping runs reproducible via saved factor/result artifacts.
- [fix] **Vibe-research plotting restored on normal department runs:** `department.md` no longer routes the `skip` gate directly into `bug_fixer` (which could mark `bug_fixer` inactive on `skip=false`). Added dedicated halt sink `dept_halt.md` and hardened `bug_fixer.md` to return `{}` when no backtest payload is present. This preserves halt short-circuiting without suppressing per-factor plot generation on active branches.
- [fix] **Custom FUND merge tolerance crash hardened:** `_run_strategy_script` safe `merge_asof` wrapper now normalizes unsupported `tolerance` inputs (notably `pd.DateOffset(months=...)`) to timedelta-compatible values, and retries without tolerance when pandas still reports incompatible tolerance. This prevents failures like `incompatible tolerance <DateOffset: months=12>` in generated factor scripts.
- [fix] **Custom strategy runtime now captures build logs and rejects empty factor frames:** `_run_strategy_script` now captures stdout/stderr during `build_factor` execution (so generated-script debug prints are attached to result payload instead of leaking to terminal), and treats empty `factor_df` as an explicit failure before persistence/backtest. This prevents misleading “factor file exists but no backtest series/plots” outcomes from silently-empty generated factors.
- [fix] **Department output contract aligned for merge/results/plots visibility:** `department` composites exit via `save_tracking`, but downstream `merge.md` expects backtest-shaped payloads (`strategy_name`, `quintiles`, `spread_q5_q1_bps`, series fields). Updated `save_tracking.md` to pass through backtest fields (including `plot_saved_path`/`plot_error`) in its `result` object while still persisting tracking and result snapshots. This restores downstream result accumulation and immediate artifact observability from the composite output path.
- [docs] **Backtest tool return schema corrected in markdown specs:** `backtest_runner.md` and `run_strategy_or_backtest.md` now correctly declare `quintiles` as an `array` (runtime returns list of quintile rows), matching `quant_lib/backtest.py`.
- [fix] **`max_factors` now caps attempts and results are persisted immediately:** `governor.md` now also stops when `len(strategies_tried) >= max_factors` (not only when successful `results` hit the cap). `merge.md` now keeps per-strategy outcomes (including failures) when `strategy_name` is present so users can see what happened each try. `save_tracking.md` now writes per-strategy result snapshots to `examples/vibe_research_md/output/results/{strategy}.json` plus rolling `latest_result_{dept}.json`.
- [fix] **Builtin strategy naming aligned with department IDs:** `_run_backtest` now passes item `name` into `quant_lib/run_backtest.py` (`--name`) and the CLI returns/uses that as `strategy_name` (and factor filename label). This prevents mismatches like `momentum_*` vs `MOM_*` in tracking, and improves immediate status stamping in `tracking_{dept}.json`.
- [feat] **One-by-one department backtesting + immediate result visibility:** Updated `iteration.md` to serialize departments as `MOM → REV → FUND` using `pass_assignment_after_prev.md`, instead of parallel fan-out. Updated `save_tracking.md` to consume `backtest_result` and immediately stamp strategy status (`success/failed`) and spread into `tracking_{dept}.json` right after each backtest. `bug_fixer` plotting remains immediate per-factor, so plots and tracking updates are available as each factor finishes.
- [fix] **FUND custom strategy path hardened (factors now persist):** `_run_strategy_script` now (1) monkey-patches `pd.merge_asof` to a safe sorting wrapper during strategy execution to prevent `left keys must be sorted`, (2) normalizes common Compustat field aliases in params (`ceq→ceqq`, `at→atq`, etc.), (3) saves custom factor DataFrames to `examples/vibe_research_md/output/factors/<strategy_name>.parquet` (matching builtin path), and (4) returns `factor_saved_path` (plus non-fatal `factor_save_error`).
- [fix] **Code sandbox exception coverage expanded:** added common exception classes (`ValueError`, `TypeError`, `KeyError`, `IndexError`, `AttributeError`) to `_ALLOWED_BUILTINS` so generated strategy scripts with standard `try/except` blocks no longer fail with `name 'ValueError' is not defined`.
- [fix] **Compustat loader backward-compat aliases:** `load_compustat()` now exposes legacy alias columns (`ceq`, `at`, `sale`, etc.) mapped from canonical quarterly names (`ceqq`, `atq`, `saleq`, ...), improving robustness for stale tracking params and older generated code.
- [feat] **Department-level plotting inside dept pipeline:** `bug_fixer.md` now generates plots immediately after each department backtest result (when `dates`, `cumulative_quintiles`, and `ls_cumulative` are present). This makes plotting happen within each department manager flow, not only in the final top-level plotting pass. Added non-fatal plot metadata (`plot_saved_path`, optional `plot_error`) to the department result payload for observability.

The old approach was fundamentally broken for multi-node sequential bodies: spread edges are snapshots, so node B can't see node A's state update via the entry's spread. New mechanism: scheduler injects scope fields into every cycle node's `inputs`, merges outputs back — ~15 lines in `_execute_node`, zero executor changes. Edge target updated from ~15 to ~5. Added `active_loop_scope_id` to `ExecutionContext`, 4 new tests (7-14 through 7-17), decisions on parallel level safety/nested loops/first-pass semantics.
- [docs] **Plan 7-6 reviewed and hardened (2 review rounds):** Resolved 8 findings: (1) scope init timing — moved from `_iterate_cycle` to `GateExecutor.execute` first call; (2) body output merge source — reads from gate's `continue_data`, no new collection mechanism; (3) iteration counter sync — scheduler writes into scope; (4) spread edge invariant — requires target port ref and landing port; (5) spread validation — skip per-field schema check; (6) markdown integration corrected — gate nodes are synthesized from `loop()` flow syntax, not standalone files; (7) `GraphMutator` + validation tasks added for spread edges; (8) 4 new tests for iteration counter, spread validation, spread resolve_inputs, flow parser.
- [docs] **Plan 7-6 node state simplification:** Created `docs/plans/7-6-node-state-simplification.md` — three backward-compatible engine changes (loop-scoped state bag, code node port defaults, struct/spread edges) to eliminate state-threading boilerplate in iterative workflows. Motivated by vibe_research analysis: 87 edges → ~5, ~500 lines of unpack/repack boilerplate eliminated. Registered as sub-plan of 7-core-hardening.
- [fix] **`edit_edge` added to `_STRUCTURAL_OPS`:** Edge endpoint rewiring via `edit_edge` now triggers entry/exit point recomputation. Previously `edit_edge` was excluded, leaving stale `entry_points`/`exit_points` when an edge was rewired.
- [fix] **Plan 10-8 post-review fixes (4 bugs from code review):** (1) Gate while-mode default ports now emit `continue`/`done` instead of `true`/`false`; `_default_ports` accepts optional `config` to select mode; `review_loop` pattern uses `continue` port and `True` condition. (2) Idempotency key scoped by `(graph_id, key)` tuple instead of global key — prevents cross-graph false hits. (3) Entry/exit point recomputation gated behind `_STRUCTURAL_OPS` set — `edit_node`/`set_position` no longer silently change entry/exit points. (4) `record_apply` metric moved after validation gate — only counts as success when the graph is actually persisted.

## 2026-02-25 (Phase 5 — decompiler review fixes)
- [fix] Decompiler now recursively writes inner agent files for `CompositeNode` sub-graphs and `ForEachNode` body sub-graphs. Previously only top-level node files were written, causing composite markdown to reference missing files and fail to recompile.
- [fix] Decompiler synthesizes a composite agent file for `ForEach` nodes with multi-node body sub-graphs (`>1` non-input nodes). The `| each()` line references the synthetic composite instead of only the first body node, preventing topology loss.
- [fix] Decompiler port emission now preserves schema and `required` values that differ from compiler defaults. Previously, default-named input/output ports were always suppressed, losing `required=True` and non-string schemas on round-trip.
- [fix] Compiler `_create_input_node` now infers output port schemas from actual target port schemas (e.g. `object`, `array`) instead of always using `string`. `InputVariable.type` remains constrained to `string|number|boolean` per the Pydantic model; the output port schema is now inferred separately.
- [fix] Decompiler escapes double-quote characters in gate conditions when emitting `| loop()` and `| if()` flow lines, preventing parse failures on recompile.
- [fix] Parser `parse_workflow_file` now collects `FlowParseError` exceptions as `parse_warnings` on `WorkflowSpec` instead of silently skipping malformed flow lines. Compiler converts these to `Diagnostic(level="warning")` with source location.
- [fix] Removed duplicate `compiler.py`/`diagnostics.py` entries in `docs/architecture.md` loader section.

## 2026-02-25 (Phase 6 — review fixes: five critical bugs)
- [fix] **`validated_composite` rewiring**: The builder helper now returns a `_ValidatedCompositeRef` proxy. When used with `>>`, inbound edges route to the entry validator and outbound edges originate from the exit validator, ensuring data always flows *through* validators instead of bypassing them.
- [fix] **RAG CRUD `_get_indexer()` uses `EmbeddingRegistry`**: Extracted shared `build_embedding_registry(config)` function in `dan/rag/__init__.py`. Both the engine's `_build_embedding_registry` and the server's `_get_indexer` now use it, honouring local and API embedding provider configurations (Option B parity).
- [fix] **Boundary validator insertion is idempotent**: `insert_boundary_validators()` now checks if `{node_id}__entry_validator` or `{node_id}__exit_validator` already exist and returns the graph unchanged, preventing duplicate node IDs and broken graphs on repeated calls.
- [fix] **Editor `addBoundaryValidators` guards on save**: The Zustand action now checks `saveGraph()` return value and aborts if the save failed, preventing API calls against stale server state.
- [fix] **Validator rule JSON editor UX**: Replaced direct `JSON.parse` on every keystroke with a `RuleConfigEditor` component using local `useState` for the textarea. Parsing and validation happen on blur, with a red border + error message for invalid JSON. Intermediate edits are preserved.
- [refactor] Consolidated `_create_embedding_provider` + `_build_embedding_registry` from `engine/scheduler.py` into `dan/rag/__init__.py` as `_create_embedding_provider` + `build_embedding_registry`. Engine delegates to the shared helper. Test monkeypatches updated.
- [test] 866 passed, 15 skipped.

Composites with custom ports (e.g. `payload`, `answer`) are correctly wired.
- [fix] **`_ValidatedCompositeRef` delegation**: Added `__getattr__` so builder methods (llm, code, etc.) inside the block delegate to the sub-workflow. Users can write `with wf.validated_composite(...) as block: block.llm(...)`.
- [test] **`test_validated_composite_flows_through_validators`**: Asserts `a >> block >> b` produces edges through entry/exit validators.

## 2026-03-20
- [docs] **Established comprehensive performance metrics and benchmark criteria framework.** Created `docs/performance-metrics-and-benchmarks.md` with four evaluation dimensions (Agent Behavior, Agent Capabilities, System Reliability, Operational Efficiency), 40+ specific metrics with target benchmarks, domain-specific benchmarks for code generation/research/conversational workflows, and integration guidelines for CI/production monitoring. Grounded in arXiv survey taxonomy [Evaluation and Benchmarking of LLM Agents: A Survey](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.21504v1) and industry best practices from [MetaDesign Solutions](https://metadesignsolutions.com/benchmarking-ai-agents-in-2025-top-tools-metrics-performance-testing-strategies/).
